Yes, this movie provides what is likely to be one of the most faithful representations of life in medieval times. And yes, that also means that everybody is covered in mud and piss and shit. Therefore yes, I hated it.

I have to admit to myself that these faux-intellectual Russian arthouse films just aren't for me. When I realized that the same dudes that wrote the book that Stalker was adapted from wrote Hard to be a God as well, I instantly knew I was in trouble. Three hour snooze fest, that's my review. Production design and cinematography are good, everything else I hated. If you like films that are long, slow, boring, have the dude doing the voiceover on screen while doing it, and a plot that is held together by the thinnest of strings, then you'll love this film!! Otherwise, avoid this like the plague.

Gimana caranya nge direct film yang aroma busuknya bisa kecium lewat layar tanpa dialog yang koheren dan gimana bisa sampe tiga jam? Gue kan nontonnya nyicil ya, per 30 menit gue istirahat, tapi makin lama 30 menitnya itu kerasa kayak 3 jam. Ga kebayang sama gue seperti apa diskusi antara orang-orang yang bisa mencerna dan menikmati film ini. Bagusnya adalah, gatau dipengaruhi oleh faktor apa, ga bikin gue ngantuk apalagi tidur!
DNF. Painfully slown. Impressive (but gross) worldbuilding. Some characters interact with the camera in intriguing ways. Pity the movie wasn't better.

Hard to Be a God is impossible to follow. In a way that I know is intentional but nonetheless made the film a laborious watch. Also, come ON having your lead look at the camera and say “It’s Hard for a God” is the most pretentious, heavy-handed, and unearned moment I’ve seen in a movie in a long while. You go hours barely engaging with the awesome concept the movie is premised on, then just have a character say it to the viewer??? I think if this were a better movie that scene could maybe work, as a Shakespearean aside kind of moment, but it definitely doesn’t do that in this film. ESPECIALLY because they do another title drop in a more traditionally shot scene with the exact same context 15 minutes later! There’s cool ideas buried in It’s Hard to be a God, but overall this is a messy, slog of a film. Sidenote: Why do a substantial number of this film’s shots look like a Hype Williams music video? Background guys jump into the center of the fish-eye lens like they’re Missy Elliot. I like the use of that perspective but some of the scenes legitimately looked too similar to influential music videos be taken as intended in this context. An odd issue to have. Two totally different artworks from different ends of the globe, but one came first so the other now carries the tonality of the other, at least for me.

Look, I tried. I made it about an hour and change into this, but I reached my limits on dudes walking around in a rainy medieval hellscape shoving all assortments of sludge into one another’s orifices. It didn’t seem like it was cohering into anything beyond that, so I tapped out. I don’t know, points for being unrelentingly weird and looking great, I guess?

i couldnt actually finish it. its an endless madhouse of a reimagined medieval society thats made up exclusively of 50 iq retards. its hard to watch past the 30 minute mark. when the initial shock of the grotesque has faded away and instead of an at least semi-coherent line of action you only get the same endless stream of creeps and lunatics, the film very quickly loses its appeal

I'd usually try to finish a movie that I've started, but I'm getting a bit tired of that recently. I ended up dropping this about 40min in. If you love consuming shit, you will love this movie. I see what it's going for, and it's an interesting idea, but I don't really feel like I get anything out of it.

More like Hard To Stay Awake. - Main guy walks up to some guy - Talk about nonsense in bad metaphors - Someone spits (kinda funny) - Someone pisses (kinda funny) - Main guy kills said guy - Repeat for 3 hours - Don’t care

I should probably watch again (as at times my attention was elsewhere), but I never will. This film is wonderfully filthy and thats about all the praise I can afford it. Overall, this was a tremendous slog - a sparse littering of memorable lines aside, this film is essentially 3 hours of medieval men trudging through mud and all manor of feces while rambling near nonsense.

Esta avaliação está longe de ter uma pontuação objetiva. Mas vou tecer um pouco a minha experiência deste filme, e acaso, quem leia, aprove os enunciados em baixo, que faça bom proveito do banquete de matéria putrefacta; Há aqui abundância de pessoas feias (disformes) sujas e deprimentes, que somente agem por via do ridiculo, do grotesco, da provocação, do repugnante, do perverso. Verdade, ou mentira 24 frames por segundo, é mais miséria e desordem em cada composição, ao ponto de eu como espectador ter vivido um pesadelo de 3h onde observava as entranhas de uma humanidade primitiva, onde a desordem e a brutalidade, aristocratas, barões, escravos, é tudo o que se conhece. Este filme descreve o inferno, assim como nos transmite, que é só o que sabemos criar, tens a perspetiva fatalista da história que nos determina condenados a cometer os mesmos erros. A narrativa é absurda até à exaustão, apesar do argumento ser interessante. Outro elemento curioso é a ausência de banda sonora, pronto nada descomunalmente atipico, mas não há grandes silêncios, a desordem é barulhenta, há constantemente ruídos de metais, gemidos, cuspidelas, gritos, pancadaria, diálogos estúpidos, risos porcos, pisadas na lama. Uma verdadeira nojeira insuportável. Bem para terminar isto, é difícil ser um deus, é a grande frase dita pelo personagem principal para se livrar do peso das ruínas geradas à sua volta, responsabilidade sua... há um documentário, talvez ele oriente noutra direção o valor retirado deste filme, é possível que o seu valor cresça quanto criação artística.

Digga es war wirklich eine Tortur 3h ekelhafte matschige, blutige, stinkende Bilder ohne einen wirklichen Sinn, eine wirkliche Message, irgendeine wirkliche Entwicklung... Robert Eggers hatte ihn als eine Inspiration für den vibe von werwulf genannt und ich hoffe, dass er wirklich nur die Sets von dem Film damit meinte und nicht irgedeinen anderen Aspekt. Weil alles andere war einfach nur sinnlos. Eine komplett überspitzte, einseitige, öde, monotone Darstellung einer mittelalterlichen Gesellschaft, die es noch nicht Mal wirklich hinbekommen hat mich zu schocken oder so. Kameraarbeit und set Design waren wirklich guut, daher kriegt der hier noch 2/5

Visually striking but narratively repetitive and unengaging to the point of dullness, which is a shame because there’s a really interesting story at play buried somewhere deep inside. The production and sound designs do a masterful job of making everything sound and feel as squishy and murky as if I’m wallowing in the filth along with the characters. While that’s to be commended, the film unfortunately often felt like it was going for gross out moments (constant and random vomiting, pissing, shitting, etc) for the sole purpose to disgust rather than to have it add anything to the story. A disappointing watch.

As aesthetically absorbing and thematically interesting as it is, Hard To Be A God is also just really long and boring and contains only the barest ghost of a story. I genuinely did not know anything had happened until the last half hour besides the lead character stumbling around drunkenly in rooms packed full of slobbering peasant mutants.
Call me an uncultured swine but I’ve got way too much water in my brain to comprehend the message that this fogslop nichemaxxing movie wanted to push on me. Would watch again!

Um filme que majoritariamente sofre pela duração. O que é um trabalho de produção inacreditável e imersivo se soma com uma premissa interessante e atuações+casting excelentes, mas se vê prejudicado por uma maneira de contar desinteressante e repetitiva. A mensagem, reflexão e sentimentos que o diretor deseja passar são, sim, muito efetivos, porém o sentimento de que o mesmo seria alcançado com um curta de 45 minutos não deixa a minha cabeça... Sujo, claustrofóbico e desolado. Principal motivo de ter assistido foi o Eggers ter informado que usou de inspiração forte pro novo filme dele e, sinceramente, mesmo sofrendo um pouco com a experiência narrativa, acredito que só podem vir inspirações positivas.

Anyone who can watch all three hours of this is genuinely a god themselves. Shitty cinematography, shitty acting (how many times can you watch men slap, shove and grab each other while random actors stare into the camera?), and a never-ending trek of rain, mud and poverty. Genuinely hard to believe in the hour of this that I watched before tapping out that the plot has anything meaningful to offer. We get it, it's a society trapped in the Middle Ages, filled with never-ending poverty and despair. What about this movie would allow the viewer to ascertain that Don Rumata is a scientist with advanced intellect from another world outside of his monologues? He and his men are just as cruel as anyone else in this world, which seems strange if his mission is to improve this society that is stuck in the dark ages. Instead, Don Rumata seems intent mostly on keeping the status quo and beating the shit out of slaves and peasants. Maybe someone who enjoys this mess can explain to me what appeal it has, because I can find as close to zero enjoyment in this movie as in any I've ever watched. Edit: Decided to finish this. I think the movie picks up a little once Reba arrests Rumata, but this movie feels like a companion piece to the original novel, so if you're like me and haven't read it, you'll have no idea what is going on at times. The cinematography isn't that bad, but it's fairly chaotic with a lot of seemingly random events happening at all times, with a sort of 360-degree view of the surrounding rooms/village squares during a scene. I don't know, I get the point for Rumata and his scientists to remain neutral and not upset the status quo, resulting in the infamous line of him saying, "it's hard to be a God" once he intervenes and begins a war that murders everyone after his wife is killed, is supposed to be poignant. However, cannot help but feel like this movie overall misses the plot elements that make the original book what it is. This is definitely an interesting interpretation/presentation of the material, but it feels incomplete to me.

No words. Just mud, dirt, and medieval vibes. What is this? I watched it with a friend, and the fun was in keeping each other watching this nonsense which we didn't finish. I might finish it sometime. Until then, here is what I want to say about it: If you're tired of fun movies, meaningful movies, bullshit movies, good movies. Or whatever other reason you might have - this movie will act as an Intermezzo, a retreat to village. no words or coherent plot. just... nothing. a masterfully crafter wind. a tasteful wind. enjoyable(?) mud. nothing makes sense, and it's absurd. as if the creator of this movie mocks me for watching it, makes it a challenge. On my first incomplete watch, i found this to be absurd nonsense. I might be missing something. It's art, but it's absurd.

Включил, потерпел и забыл. Агрессивно-навязчивое занудство. Впервые за всю карьеру Алексея Германа его картина выглядит такой бессильной. Впредь буду делать вид, что в фильмографии великого режиссера этого фильма нет.
There's a lot too much messiness here, both literally and figuratively. I found it visually fascinating with dense and, at times, incomprehensible writing.

Hard to Be a God a tout pour me plaire : graphique, intense, chaotique, sale… mais seulement après deux heures de visionnage. Avant ça, les deux premières heures introduisent un monde dense et brutal de manière apparement volontairement monotone, et désolé… moi je me suis fait chier, j’aime pas ça. Genre, donnez-moi du sang direct je sais pas. Et les dialogues sérieux… les ruskov, on comprend rien à ce qu’ils racontent ces enfoirés.

there's probably some artistic dimension of vulgarity that can be found from the " visually astonishing " masterpiece of Hard to Be a God , where you can witness shit, smell shit and lick shit out of a peasant's dirty butt cheeks. embrace the reality of life in Russia. if that's your thing, this is probably your Bible. honestly, it's something that Béla Tarr would likely handle with somber grace. but, as seems to be the case with Aleksei German, once you've seen 20 minutes you've seen it all. this should be an art installation where you can taste authentic manure and bathe in mud. not exactly my fetish, though: 3 hours of literal horseshit is like 20 hours of Sátántangó , 10 hours of Inland Empire or 1 hour of Hereditary . if Hard to Be a God makes you thrive, you're either a) a pretentious cunt, or b) a true champion of cinema... and in that case I salute you, you sick fuck.

The book changed my life. The feelings of solace, desolation, and disparaging hope, are all present in this clearly Russian film. It does well to reflect of the fact that any action made by the protagonist is inconsequential through the style of filming. The camera moves independently of Romatta, showing the life and landscape, reflecting ever-moving history. He has and will have no lasting effect on the planet and its people. Great ideas to get a broader scope. Look up the Strugatsky's and the challenges they struggled with to get this published.

If Monty Python and the Holy Grail took a generous dose of extraterrestrial heroin and experienced a vile, demented, and chaotic reverie of itself in black and white I did not like this. It was a struggle getting through its 3 hour drone of pure filth and gore that ultimately amounts to nothing in my opinion The acting, costumes, and set designs are pretty great though

Mindenek előtt leszögezném, hogy ezt a filmet egyszer látni kell, mert technikai szempontból lenyűgöző. Mármint abban az értelemben, hogy egy film erre képes. Lehetséges ezt létrehozni, felépíteni, megcsinálni.  Ugyanakkor, felmerül a kérdés, hogy mi végre épült ez a szerkezet, mit akartak mondani vele, mi indokolja? Ugyanis a második óra után nézőként rá kellett jönnöm, hogy a mondanivaló, amire ez a 177 perc épül, nagyon vékony. (Költői kérdésként pedig gyorsan  feltenném, hogy amúgy meg lehet-e úszni bűntetlenül, ha egy moziban háromszor is belemondják a film címét a kamerába?) Értem, az egyes frakciók sosem nyugszanak, és mindig lesznek szürkék, akiknek nem tetszenek a feketék, de amúgy bármikor jöhetnek fehérek, akik meg a másik kettővel akarnak leszámolni. Valaki mindig hatalomra akar kerülni, valakit mindig le kell kaszabolni. Az öldöklés sosem érhet véget. Ez az állítás lehet igaz, de nem kell különösebben okosnak lenni egy ilyen tézis kigondolásához és pláne nem kell 177 perc ennek elmondására. Hogy honnan tudom? Láttam már más filmeket is. A játékidőt esetleg indokolhatja, hogy German ezzel akarja érzékeltetni, hogy a változás sosem következik be és mindig minden ugyanúgy marad: köpködés, hányás, vér, belek, ebéd, majd szarás. Ez a rendezői vízió. Mert ez maximum az. German nem épít világot, csak ügyesen elhazudja azt. A logikátlan dolgokkal telezsúfolt terek ügyesen elhitetik a nézőkkel, hogy amit látnak az egy alternatív univerzum, de igazából olyanok ezek a díszletek, mintha nem lenne ott semmi, mert funkciótlan és felesleges. Ahogy a szereplőket, úgy a nézőt is csak akadályozzák. Egy világ építéséhez szükség lenne arra is, hogy a szereplőket néha lássuk nevetni, tudjuk mit találnak esetleg szépnek, milyen amikor nem ölik egymást, vagy épp nincsenek iszonyatosan bebaszva. Ja, és esetleg a nők és a gyerekek is komolyabb szerephez jutnának, de legalább egynél többnek lehetne szöveges szerepe, amiből jellemet tud építeni magának. És esetleg lassan a környezet és annak szabályai is kibontakozhatnának előttünk. Ezek nélkül csak vízióról, sőt rosszabb esetben üres vízióról beszélünk. A film narrátora ugyan hozzánk vág néhány fogodzkodónak szánt izét, de hogy ki, mikor, mit és hol és miért, az nem derül ki belőle. Szerintem kb. 45 percig nem tudtam ki az a Rumata. De utána sem tudtam, hogy ki kicsoda. Értem, hogy itt cél volt, hogy eltávolodjanak a sci-fi bevett formáitól, csak a film nem indokolja meg ennek az okát. Azt sem, hogy miért kellett ehhez a Sztrugackij-regény? Egy idő után minden csak gimmické silányul. Még a fényképezés egyes megoldásai is (pl.: hogy rendszerint emberek nyúlnak a képbe, tárgyakat lógatnak be stb.), pedig abban van a legtöbb invenció. German egyszerre használja úgy a kamerát, mint egy dokumentumfilmes, meg úgy, mintha egy szereplő lenne, máskor pedig mint egy hideg, objektív külső tekintetet. Ahogy a kamera időnként megjelenik a térben borzasztó izgalmas. Meg az a sok lélegzet elállító kép is, ami van ebben a filmben! Kár, hogy csak az marad meg belőle, hogy mennyire szétkínozza a nézőt, mert nem sikerül mélyre mennie. De lehet, hogy ez az egyik állítása: hogy nem is lehet. De megint csak tippelgetek.

In which scientists arrive on another planet that's several centuries behind ours (a permanent dark ages where intellectuals are killed) and get lost in a peculiar art house murk that is noteworthy for being one of the grossest movies ever made (nary a scene goes by unmarked by spit, urine, or worse). Aleksei German shot Hard to Be A God from 2000-2006 and it wasn't completed and released until after his death. The long production process is evident: at times it's stunning and the attention to detail in conjuring up this humid, disgusting savage world is admirable. So, I can't write if off completely. And if you can warm up to three hours of a nearly impossible to follow narrative and the belligerent perversity of it all, go for it. There are a few visually arresting moments where I thought maybe a masterpiece could seep out, but ultimately this left me as cold as fish in milk.

Pretty tight to put on as a visualizer while listening to doom metal. Couldn’t tell you a single thing that happened in it. Big movie for people who think protracted shots of fuck all happening is “poetic” or whatever. If you want to watch people rolling around in shit you could just go to burning man, but I guess that wouldn’t make you feel more justified in getting an English degree.

This took me four days to watch the whole thing cause I could not care for this whatsoever oopsss. For all its technical prowess (with the film mostly composed of insane long-takes and scarily complicated compositions that are undeniably outstanding), it lost me in its overwhelming grim and filthiness. Dirt, mud, rain, sweat, spit, blood, piss, vomit, you name it, it was all here, and without any rhyme or reason other than a feeble attempt at portraying this otherworldly planet as dopey cretins and moronic barbarians. The main performance lowkey aggravated me and his face was annoying (IDGAF) and just the overall atmospheric shitscape and absurdist caricatures did not vibe with me whatsoever. You could argue that the film is trying to disturb you and make you uncomfortable, especially with its muddy scenery and grotesque actions, but it kinda morphed from the initial intended disgust of the into a neverending, painstaking emotion deprivation (in other words, i was bored) alongside being just frustrated and mad at some points, especially when the characters cartoonishly address the camera in a seemingly meaningless and pandering demeanor. I didn’t like this SORRY !

A film ignorant to it’s viewers existence. Hard to be a god is a film that I went into with high expectations, it was reviewed well by critics I respect and it was compared by a few to films such as David Lynch’s “Inland Empire” a title I hold to a very high regard. So you can imagine my disappointment when after the first hour a realisation started to set in; that although this film has great atmosphere and sets, it’s cryptic dialogue and seemingly nonsensical plot progression will not be to it’s aid in telling a story and it will inevitably exhaust me. (It did) This is a shame, as I enjoy films which require figuring out to understand, but the level of ambiguity is inherently detrimental towards the viewing experience and makes the film feel like it hates its viewers. It is a shame that I say this, as this was a massive passion project for the director who clearly had a vision that I respect greatly, but sadly it just does not resonate with me.

И наверное, неспроста ты, блять, оказался в той ситуации, в которой оказался. Знаешь, это конечно, плохо, но, блять, Бог тебя пристроил, как говорится. Это твоё почётное место отныне и навсегда. Вот ты раньше был говно, а щас ты сидишь в говне. Ты сидишь там, где тебе место. К сожалению, как ни прискорбно, блять, но это так я книгу не читал, не понял ни хуя. мама книгу читала, поняла чуть больше, чем нихуя. сказала, вайб вообще мимо. верю на слово. возможно что-нибудь стало бы понятно, если б хотя бы пару-тройку реплик можно было расслышать. а так получается что Ярмольник три часа бессмысленно бродит по говну, в камеру постоянно пихают говно, приговаривая "глядите-ка — говно! воняет, не правда ли?". и в конце Ярмольник осознаёт, что говно — это действительно говно, и нахуй всех убивает (за кадром). шедевр, браво. зелёный слоник отдыхает. но, конечно, нельзя отрицать, что была проделана огромная работа
Filme baseado naquela cena do filme do Laboratório de Dexter em que eles vão pro futuro distante q o Mandark virou o Overlord e proibiu a inteligência

This movie is the cinematic equivalent of painting the an intricate religious icon with nothing but feces, urine, vomit, pus and spit. Though it has an interesting premise, it is a rather slow paced experiece of watching nothing but disgusting Russian men doing the grossest things imaginable while mumbling uncertainties and some philosophical rants when they are with drunk or drugged. I understand the intent of the movie, but it has a clearly nihilistic and incorrect view of how we see the middle ages. But since Robert Eggers said his team watched this film's aesthetics for his upcoming "Werwulf", I am gratefu to have seen what I will admit is one of the most important movies to watch as a cinephile.

Hard to Be a God drinking game: take a sip every time someone’s face gets smeared in either blood or shit. Same reaction I had to the novel: great concept and some very interesting themes rendered in a story I had no clue how to follow. This film version specifically really doesn’t take any advantage of the sci-fi elements of the premise, doubling down on the dirty medieval vibes. Not inherently against that but I needed more than that to be onboard for 3 hours.

HTBAG (which feels sacrilegious to abbreviate) suffers for the same reason why yves klein/rothko are not my favorite artists - sure it’s technically impressive that you made something that blue/red/viscera and shit and rain and mud and blood-suffused, but it’s still painting with one hue.

2,5 hours nothing really happens. during the two hour exposition there are some short rather schematic events. around two hours in they start making puns on god and clumsily play on the main metaphor. cinematography consists of erratic close-ups with constant visual noise. mud, dirt, blood, piss, shit, saliva, sweat, rainwater in frames are in constant material flux. everyone is constantly throwing something, slapping, hitting and pushing each other, touching with a point of a spear or a knife, pulling one‘s nose. my sense of spatial privacy was in shock. cloth rustles, weapons jingle, armor shines. additionally there is performative murmuring and mumbling all the way. the (re)ception of middle ages is that of an attentive bachtin reader. fog and smoke translate single objects into one another. because of the setting there are no „natural“ set locations: every single one of the props was collected separately and then arranged for every scene to make the effect of a pile. as a result people are perceived as being treated like things too, especially towards the last third of the movie. male power fantasies of being rich noble castle dwellers in the middle ages owning slaves, peasant women and capital: colonising a less developed land unable to defend itself. the same people speak about renaissance and progress. jesus got crucified, but don rumata is an executioner himself. the ending hints rather at the old testament tyrant. by extending the metaphor on aristocracy and the whole middle age social hierarchy the concept of god is degraded to that of a well-born well-doing in comparison to the others: a “great man” in the worst (renaissance) sense of the word, just one powerful enough to do atrocities accompanied by loud words and have no punishment whatsoever. how hard indeed.

Mongolito, quand tu baves, c'est rigolo ! Bon j'avais un peu de temps, je suis allé voir ça, le pitch avait l'air sympa, ça faisait penser à Stalker... normal, c'est adapté d'un bouquin des mêmes auteurs... Je rentre dans la salle et c'est long, franchement c'est long... J'aurai aimé dire que le film me reste à l'esprit et me parle même une fois dehors, comme ça peut arriver des films qui hantent et qui obligent à reconsidérer le premier visionnage, mais ce n'est même pas le cas. J'adore l'idée de base, une autre planète coincée dans une sorte de Moyen-âge, ils ont empêché la renaissance de se produire... et on suit ces personnages avec des plan séquences qui ne sont pas laids, loin de là (enfin quoique, la salle (toute petite) était bondée, j'étais au second rand, le nez collé à l'écran et la projection numérique c'est immonde à cette distance, l'image du grain et tu vois les sortes de pixel sur l'écran ça pique !), mais en fait la même scène tourne en boucle pendant 2h50, alors si on rentre dans le truc je suis certain que l'on peut trouver ça magnifique, mais si comme moi on regarde ça de dehors, ben 2h50, c'est 2h50 et c'est long. Je ne dirai pas que c'est ennuyant, mais c'est long, on regarde ça montre quoi... En fait ça manque d'intérêt, d'émotions, c'est trop tout le temps... ça n'ose pas tout simplement se poser et filmer ces gens là, faut toujours faire pleins de mouvements de caméras dans tous les sens... Je pense également que le Moyen-âge ne devait pas en être très loin niveau crasse, mais là vu comme c'était filmé ça faisait quand même un peu caricature et ça lasse, c'est toujours la même chose. L'intrigue de base passe totalement au second plan pendant tout le film pour suivre ces bouseux vivre leur vie pestilentielle ! C'est triste quoi. Un film que j'ai déjà oublié en fait... sans que ça soit mauvais, je comprends qu'on puisse accrocher, les quelques plans où il filme les décors naturels c'est pas mal parce que ça fait dans la simplicité et pas dans l'esbroufe, le surplus, on est dans l'épure. Je pense par exemple au plan final. J'ai cependant bien aimé le truc pour promener les prisonniers, une sorte de véhicule où tous les gens sont attachés à une corde et s'ils tombent ben ils meurent pendus. La sélection naturelle en somme. Faut peut-être le voir comme une curiosité. Pour ma part j'irai sans doute voir la première adaptation du bouquin qui sera peut-être moins bordélique.

Medieval sci-fi. It was a disgusting and immersive experience into what a world, pre-scientific revolution, would look like. It was aight. Lots of pissing and shitting, awkward close ups and just nastiness. Makes sense for the time period and it was stylistically interesting but beyond that I just couldn't get into it.

Through a sensory odyssey primarily consisting of what you just know is the colour brown, even though it's in black and white, a look at absolute stagnation where humanity finds itself at a grim evolutionary dead-end if history was to have taken a different wrong turn and come to a dead stop. At the same time, it is hard to imagine how in the admittedly hyper-specific circumstances of asking someone to parody the grimmest, largely humourless (the protagonist gets a finger poked up his nose at one point) Russian art film of religious metaphor largely as rolling around in a giant pigsty that they could imagine, they'd come up with anything too different. As every surface is coated in mud and blood and every sky completed obscured by grey fog with the very distinct roaming camerawork pressing itself right up into it, it's no exaggeration to call this one of the most overwhelmingly filthy movies ever made, turning a world essentially based on our historical past into an almost unrecognisable as human hellscape. You're done with the sound of sinuses by the end of the first fifteen minutes. It is undoubtedly one of those films with such a self-assured textural style that very little else will look like it, and the one primary thing it seeks to get across mixed in of course with the Stalinist critiques of the murder of intellectuals barring all routes for advancement seems to be to ask what a non-interventionist god could even do for a world that humanity has driven into a hole. It shows vignette after vignette of people being dumb and cruel and an observing god who is burned out and exhausted by it, isolated in a world beyond help. It seems to argue that global progress is not guaranteed, that the world is not inevitably destined to get better over time if we just negligently sit back to let it, which in might make this a compelling dark mirror image of a worst possible scenario lest we not work to avoid it if you choose to view it so. By basing its entire being in a three-hour quagmire though of mostly passive observance, it creates a storytelling impasse. Where something like On the Silver Globe might show the maddened cycle of civilisation, this shows through its similarly vivid design the existential flatline where progress is stunted, and it's hard to get away from that being quite boring. Worse still this actually quite straightforward to describe structure and character pitch is delivered incomprehensibly by its actual script speaking in what largely amounts to nonsense and non sequiturs, and these political and philosophical ideas might be actually more palpable if its story wasn't so deliberately obtuse and intent on keeping its world abstract. By the end of the first hour we've basically learned very little about its characters that we're following and its factions and forces, and for the most part for the next two that's where it stays, a contextless tour of a mucky, mucky place. It plods through these various encounters that purposefully don't amount to much as progression is antithetical, and it often comes off bumbling as much as it does horrific, a great realisation of a setting but with thin, ponderous storytelling within it. It's certainly somewhat hypnotic through its pure verisimilitude, but not especially interesting. Definitely a vibe and an achievement, but honestly that should be more moving.

This film is 3 hours of absolute mayhem and carnage. The film is about a group of humans who get sent to another planet with humans, but these ones are stuck in the Middle Ages basically. So the Earth humans have to integrate themselves with the populous and make sure that they are able to get through these dark times. We follow one of these Earth humans know has ‘Don Rumata’. At no point did I feel like the Don Rumata was doing his job and why he came to the planet in the first place. To help this civilization evolve. It felt like he was just abusing everyone and being a complete menace. He takes method acting to a whole new level 😂. It’s quite clear that he has immersed himself so much that he’s really living the lie. Leonid Yarmolnik, the actor who plays Don Rumata, gives a phenomenally true and outlandish performance. He was great. I could see an argument for watching this with subtitles OFF. They provided basically no help in terms of what was happening. The only upside is that quite a bit of the dialogue is funny and some of it can be surprisingly profound. Honestly I got more understanding of the story from one of the old Lego games, where there’s no dialogue and just grunting. It’s like the actors were told the beginning and the end of a scene and then told to just improvise the rest. To be honest, to begin with, it was a tough watch because of how nonsensical it is. The production is crazy good and completely immersive. There are few films that are at this level in terms of that aspect. It’s muddy and mucky everywhere, everyone is covered in piss and shit. Every part of the film feels so alive. As if they really created a fully fictional medieval village and told all the extras to go about their jobs whilst the film was happening. There’s a part where someone’s guts get spilled out and then his whole chest comes away and you see a still beating heart. Some guy literally gets dragged by a horse during a scene. There are also so many times where someone will just get shat on midway through a scene 😂 The film is shot in a documentary style. The amount of times a scene will be happening and some dude will just walk across the frame, looking directly down the lens the whole time. So funny. Because of the documentary hand held style the camera work is really interesting. The camera is constantly moving and it feels like the film has very few cuts. The editing is pretty good in that regard too. There isn’t really any worrying about if something is slightly obscuring the shot or if the lens is covered in blood or crap. That being said though, towards the end, during a pivotal scene, someone is blocking the majority of the fame. I think someone from behind the camera calls out (not heard) the actors look, wait (someone says wait), the person blocking the frame moves slightly and then the actors continue with the scene. Like nothing happened 😂. I watched this in two sittings. I don’t know whether the second half is better or, if me having a sleep made me enjoy it more. Honestly though, once you just accept it for what is it, there’s so much humour in its wackyness and uniqueness. Below is just a few of my favourite quotes/passages of dialogue from this film: “Don Rumata, the empires best swordsman. 186 duals but not a single kill. Only their ears. 372 ears in total.” “Maybe the Abyss belched you out? Maybe you’re the son of god?” “The fact that I’m talking to you… doesn’t necessarily mean we’re having a conversation” “Don’t get mad Don. Have a potato” - “What would you do if you were a god?” - “I wouldn’t have any problems urinating” (Don proceeds to pour out his water flask to help the man - the man later urinates on Don) “Creator, if you exist, blow us away like dust or pus. Or leave us to rot like we are. Destroy us all. Destroy everyone.” “Get out, everyone. I’m going to wash my arse” “I saw you blowing snot today” “If you write about me, and you’ll probably have to… write that… it’s hard to be a god”

Está sempre acontecendo alguma coisa, mas nada acontece. Mais ou menos como a nossa história no planeta Terra. Como já falaram aqui, é realmente um filme enfadonho, cansativo de acompanhar, dada a fragilidade, ou quase ausência, de narrativa (que ainda permanece bastante inacessível para mim - vou atrás do livro). Tive que terminar no dia seguinte. Ao mesmo tempo, é uma das produções mais impressionantes e hipnóticas que já vi. Um trabalho sem igual de produção de arte: não há um canto da tela que escape, tudo está transmitindo a mensagem, tudo transborda o universo do filme. Parece até que a tela é pequena demais, e as coisas e as pessoas se espremem para aparecer nela. A impressão de improviso em boa parte das atuações, ao invés de diminuir ou quebrar a nossa crença no que está sendo apresentado, incrivelmente a reforça, levando o filme quase ao nível de documentário. Se tem a impressão de muita verdade. Também me peguei pensando, enquanto assistia, que passamos boa parte da nossa vida lidando com o desconforto, com a bagunça, com a decadência do ambiente em que vivemos e do nosso próprio corpo, com a sujeira e com a putrefação, numa luta sem fim para nos mantermos vivos, limpos, confortáveis e minimamente apresentáveis. Uma luta que leva do nada a lugar nenhum, cíclica, zerada a todo o amanhecer. Com exceção daquele único, último dia, em que lutamos pela última vez, e perdemos. E sabemos que vamos perder, mas é preciso travar essa luta, ainda assim.

383/500 Aleksei German’s Hard to Be a God is an immersive and miasmic experience that chooses textural storytelling over traditional narrative. Within the first few minutes, excrement has been thrown, and you must decide for yourself whether you’re in or out. The filth doesn’t end there: German’s entropic odyssey festers with pestilence, decay, rot, and offal, all caught within the claustrophobic framework of Ilin and Klimenko’s somnambulant cinematography. Hands in the camera; piss, shit, and spit just being thrown at you for three hours straight—it’s a complete indifference to the audience and to the film’s subjects. But that indifference is the point. Ilin, Klimenko, and German visualize an authoritarian society where there is no personal space; life clambers on top of itself, everyone preying on everyone else just to survive. It’s a direct reflection of the Stalinism that German’s family lived through. Hard to Be a God is constantly reminding us that there is no dignity in authoritarian societies. Rumata starts the film as a passive observer, believing he can watch the cruelty and stupidity around him without joining it, hoping to influence society through behavior modification. By the end, he realizes he can’t, and that he’s as guilty as everyone else of contributing to the moral rot of Arkanar society. In a world devoid of purpose and meaning, ennui and cruelty consume everyone and everything; and passivity becomes its own sort of violence.

I came for the interesting premise, but stayed for the prolonged claustrophobia, snorts and farts, and depravity. Three hours full of shots with meat hooks or ropes hanging in the middle of the screen, incredibly oddly crowded rooms and fast-paced, short dialogues. All the while you're unable to make sense of all that's happening, and are entertained with beautiful photography and unique cinematography that seems to deliberately break every rule of film. This is an incredible experience, unbelievably perplexing and even funny. This is close to a masterpiece.

Paradoxalmente, uma das reprentações mais acuradas da Idade Média depois de "Andrei Rublev" (Tarkovsky, 1966), "É Difícil ser um Deus" (Aleksei German, 2013) não é diretamente sobre o medievo terrestre, mas sim o de um outro planeta chamado Arkanar. Alegoricamente, é também sobre o terrestre, claro. E não é nada agradável de se ver; ao invés de romantizar esse período da História humana, German retrata-o como um antro de sujeira e iniquidade. É necessário um notável esforço de atenção para compreender o que se passa, pois captamos apenas fragmentos. Ao invés de um plot tradicional, com fases narrativas bem delineadas e personagens imbuídos de motivações claras, o diretor propõe uma experiência sensorial. Um pouco como no cinema de Béla Tarr, somos postos diante de um continuum em que o lento desdobrar do tempo tem de ser sentido, ao lado da materialidade palpável de lugares e pessoas. Em planos longos, a câmera flutua pelas ruas e interiores de casas, criando um efeito de imersão no universo camponês mais lúgubre que você já viu. An Earth scientist, ensconced undercover as a demi-god nobleman on the planet Arkanar, which is populated by humans whose development has become stuck in the Middle Ages due to being in the grips of a violently anti-intellectual dictatorship, slowly begins to lose his mind and "go native" as he gets ever more involved in pushing Arkanar into the Enlightenment Age. Or... at least I think that's what the movie is about.  It's difficult to figure out as the film de-emphasizes plot in favor of plunging the viewer into a hellish, shit caked medieval world for 3-hours.  The director's use of documentary-style POV makes you feel like you're constantly in the thick of it as you follow the main character around, getting jostled around by the filthy inhabitants of this world as they grin in your face with idiotic and maniacal smiles.  The effect almost makes it feel like the filmmakers truly traveled back in time to document the toil and drudgery of medieval life. That being said, this movie is a hard, *hard* watch.  What little story that is meted out is difficult to follow, and the sci-fi concept of Earthling observers studying this planet is so downplayed as to be practically non-existent to the plot.  It's hard for me to imagine the main character, and the other Earth scientists, have ever been anything other than Arkanar natives (perhaps that is the point).  Still, some hint of their advanced technology and intelligence might  have been an interesting contrast to the rest of the visuals of the movie. Speaking of which, the production design is staggering in its detail to reproduce an authentic medieval experience.  Again, it feels like the filmmakers shot on location in the Middle Ages, which is an incredible feat in and of itself.

Não demora muito para que, vendo É DIFÍCIL SER UM DEUS (2013), a gente desista logo de entender a trama e se permita viajar na força onírica de suas imagens. Há quem diga que é porque o livro no qual o filme é baseado é de difícil adaptação, mas é possível que o cineasta russo Aleksey German não tenha se preocupado muito com esse tipo de detalhe. Seu filme-testamento, em nenhum momento, procura ser fácil para o espectador, foi feito como que numa delírio. O fato de ter quase três horas de duração também não ajuda muito o trabalho a ser apreciado por espectadores apressados e impacientes. É preciso paciência e uma reeducação do olhar para que essas imagens poderosas sejam não só apreciadas, mas recebidas com maravilhamento e assombro, misturado também a algum asco provocado por cenas violentas ou de causar repulsa mesmo, como pessoas com o nariz pingando, com feridas expostas ou imagens de cadáveres pendurados ou vísceras à mostra, num espetáculo tão perturbador que esquece-se que são efeitos especiais. Talvez o preto e branco das imagens passe essa impressão de verdade. É DIFÍCIL SER UM DEUS é um dos trabalhos mais importantes da carreira de German, contemporâneo de Andrei Tarkovski, e que morreu antes de ver sua obra finalizada. German passou quatro décadas idealizando, doze anos filmando e faleceu em 2013, deixando a edição e a finalização para seu filho e sua esposa, ambos colaboradores de longa data da produção. Felizmente é um desses trabalhos bem especiais, que oferecem ao espectador uma experiência única, que vai além do gostar ou do não gostar. Independentemente disso, saímos da sessão diferentes. É DIFÍCIL SER UM DEUS se passa em um universo semelhante à nossa Idade Média em alguns países da Europa, mas há algo de muito estranho que nos leva a acreditar que se trata de um mundo novo e estranho. E na verdade se trata de um outro planeta, como é dito no início, nos letreiros de apresentação. Ver o filme no cinema ou ao menos em uma tela maior é essencial para que os vários planos gerais e os ricos detalhes da direção de arte e a bela fotografia em preto e branco sejam vistos com mais clareza. É, definitivamente, um filme para ser assistido no cinema, por mais difícil que seja sua exibição comercial. Tanto é que até agora ele permanece inédito em nosso circuito. Pude vê-lo em uma mostra dedicada a filmes ousados esteticamente e arriscados comercialmente, a Mostra Cinema em Transe, exibida em Fortaleza no mês de janeiro. O curioso de ler a sinopse de É DIFÍCIL SER UM DEUS é não encontrar exatamente o que é descrito na tela. Na trama, um grupo de cientistas é enviado ao planeta Arkanar para ajudar a civilização local, que está passando por uma fase ainda muito rudimentar de sua história, a encontrar o seu caminho para o progresso. A missão é difícil, já que eles não podem interferir violentamente e nem matar aquelas pessoas. O cientista Rumata tenta salvar os intelectuais locais de uma punição. Essa é mais ou menos a sinopse meio maluca e resumida que aparece no IMDB. Na confusa história que acompanhamos na tela, que é o que importa, afinal, já que a obra cinematográfica precisa ser analisada de modo independente da obra literária, vemos um homem de aparência quase gigante e considerado um deus pelos demais. Aos nossos olhos ele só parece superior aos demais por ser maior, mais forte, se vestir diferente e principalmente por não estar coberto de lama. Os demais mais parecem porcos vivendo em um chiqueiro. A lama é uma constante e está presente em quase todo o filme. Ainda que adaptado da obra literária dos mestres da ficção científica russa Arkady e Boris Strugatsky, que também serviram de inspiração para uma das obras mais aclamadas de Tarkovski, STALKER, o filme de German brinca muito com as possibilidades que só o cinema é capaz, como a aproximação um tanto exagerada da câmera nos rostos e corpos dos atores, ou a própria maneira como eles lidam com essa câmera, chegando, em alguns momentos, a falar com ela. É o tipo de obra que cobra muito do espectador, mas que recompensa muito bem aqueles dispostos a irem até o fim em sua difícil travessia. I remember sitting on my friends dorm room floor and buying this for 4 dollars nearly a decade ago. Ever since then it has been on my Mount Everest of films alongside the act of killing and an elephant sitting still, films that I know I need to watch but are extremely difficult and grueling. I’m still not sure if I like this film, but I really loved the themes and imagery. Given that the director spent decades trying to make this in Soviet Russia, it brilliantly shows how rampant ant-intellectualism will ultimately lead a society to live in a world filled with piss, shit, blood, mud, spit, snot, and an overall grime that makes you as nihilistic as the main character. The audio design was incredible and if I recall correctly, the entire film is dubbed audio, making all of the disgusting noises of mud and dripping water even more unnerving. Before last night I had probably tried to watch this more than a dozen times. This leads me to my main criticism: despite having watched the first ~90 minutes so many times, I still had no idea what was going on. This film isn’t for everyone, but it is an unforgettable experience.

more shit, piss and blood in this than any movie i've ever seen. wildly disorienting movie. not just on the level of plot which is enjoyably vague but the entire approach of the movie is designed to alienate and disgust the viewer. extras bump into the camera or stare directly at it, random hands enter the frame during long takes, often with no apparent reason. there's a claustrophobic squalor that's as repulsive as it is fascinating. funny that for a movie technically set on another planet this feels like the most realistic representation of the middle ages in cinema. thematically it's also about as bleak as it gets: our suffering is intractable, we are all victims of slow moving progress, etc. honestly, it's a masterpiece.

3 Stunden in der Hölle. Perfektes Worldbuilding. Ich habe noch nie einen Film gesehen, der eine bestimmte Epoche so plastisch und unangenehm detailliert darstellt. Schlamm, Regen, Scheiße und Aas machen den Großteil des Inhalts aus, die Kamera bewegt sich wie im Freiflug, schwerelos wie ein unsichtbarer Dokumentator durch die Gegend und geht dabei teilweise so nah an ihre Motive heran, dass man sie praktisch riechen kann. Robert Eggers meets Béla Tarr, nur dass Ersterer sich wahrscheinlich in den Schlaf weint, weil der Film genau das erreicht, was er seit Jahren versucht zu replizieren. Unglaublich, dass sich der Film nicht wie eine Geduldsprobe anfühlt, dafür dass eigentlich kaum etwas passiert. Wir sehen nur wie Rumata durch die Gegend streift und durchgehend seine Untertanen schikaniert, durch den guerilla-dokumentarischen Stil wirkt das aber ungeahnt spannend. Ein unfassbar deprimierender und bösartiger Film.

Сильные вайбы Белы Тарра. Грязь, моральное разложение, вечное несчастье и сумасшествие. Актёры так же порадовали. Ярмольник в этой роли вообще прекрасно смотрится, она ему очень подходит, как по мне. Hard to Be a God takes you through a world where people look directly into the camera and objects are constantly dangled in front of it, while faces and hands appear from nowhere like the lens is another person trying to make its way through each brutal scene. I absolutely love it and these are some Sunday morning ramblings as to why. The main character, Rumata, goes through a constant bombardment of requests and threats, alongside the filth and brutality of the society he is in. But for most of the film he takes almost everything in his stride, like he's super calm regardless of what mess is happening. He knows another kind of civilisation is possible and knows that something needs to change, but that doesn't mean he can do anything on his own. So he's kind of stuck in a perpetual cycle of guts and grime; back and forth with piss, snot and puddles and random machines and spikes and musical instruments and fog. But in spite of that, I never felt the film lacked 'progress' because I never really got why 'progress' needs to mean moving in a tidy way from one point to another. Life doesn't really work that way, or maybe it does for some folks, but it doesn't for social and technological development, despite how we might think that it does. Rumata basically continues living in this world where everything is interrupted and familiar problems return, with the Renaissance he knows could happen staying somewhere on the horizon beyond the moonshine, zits and donkey penises. The filthiness is probably pushed a bit too far, and 3 hours of hawking and traipsing through sludge, alongside lacerated butt cheeks and dead fish, totally becomes an endurance test - but that was also part of the fun. I didn't find it repetitive because the filmmaker finds so many different ways of presenting this world, particularly through the movement of the camera and the awesome use of props. It is disgusting and obscene, but it also has moments of despair and grief for characters whose lives I got interested in without necessarily identifying with them. The Baron, for instance, waving his sword around like a raging loon before ending up face down with arrows in his back was especially brutal. He had so much more to give! The film also left me thinking about a society where few people seem capable of imagining that things could be different, while Rumata knows that they can be and still can't work out how to make that change happen. His knowledge and his $$$ distinguishes him from the people around him, but he's not really superior cos he still spits and flings donkey poop, increasingly behaving like someone who belongs in that time and place. The thing that makes him different is that he knows another world is possible, while the film gradually tests how much that knowledge is worth when he can't create it himself. By the time he goes berserk and loses his restraint, the hours beforehand validate his spree, and I found the whole thing fascinating and totally unforgettable.

Civilization feels less like a promise than a distant illusion, swallowed by a world drowning in mud, cruelty, and endless decay. Every frame is suffocatingly alive, overflowing with bodies, filth, noise, and violence until history itself begins to resemble a nightmare without beginning or end. Rather than observing chaos from a safe distance, the film forces you to inhabit it, stripping away every trace of comfort as if humanity were trapped inside its own moral decomposition. Its greatness lies in the relentless conviction of its vision. Power, knowledge, and progress are rendered almost meaningless against the weight of ignorance and brutality, turning the story into something far larger than science fiction or historical allegory. It is an overwhelming meditation on the impossibility of redemption in a world unwilling to change, demanding endurance as much as attention. ★★★★★ — a monumental descent into the abyss of human barbarity, where history rots in plain sight and even gods are powerless before mankind.

“I can see, but it feels like I can’t.” The closest I’ll ever come to knowing what it must feel like to be schizophrenic. An onslaught of audio/visual mud both literal and metaphorical. Once I gave up trying to understand what was going on and just let myself exist as an observer in this hellish landscape, it all started to feel hypnotic and oddly profound. In a world where there is no sense to be made – no order, no social norms – an idiot on a leash babbling formless incoherencies can begin to feel like an oracle for the divine. A film I will never forget without a single scene I will ever remember.

A wonderfully ingenious and aesthetically appealing display of stop-motion animation — and, to me, little else. Guillermo del Toro ’s Pinocchio strikes me as a frustrating waste of technical prowess — namely, the visual presentation and impeccable animation work — with such tepid, handholding material beneath the charming carapace. While worthy and multifaceted topics are indeed tackled, they are done so with no novelty whatsoever (beyond the aesthetic) and mostly with the depth of an entirely unremarkable children’s story. The subject of death is handled somewhat better by the end, but at that stage the damage was all done. With a slew of obnoxiously obvious allegories and a cartoonish simulacrum of fascism, the film attempts to juggle far too much for its feebly thin central storyline to handle; and these characters are so numbingly banal and paper-thin, I couldn’t care enough to get invested in them. Pinocchio himself is an obnoxious embodiment of the ‘innocent outsider can’t comprehend evil’ trope, which is neither new nor interesting when this barebones, and his relationship with Geppetto is as uninspired and one-dimensional. The Cricket is a perplexingly unimportant piece of the puzzle, and when he’s not around it’s easy to forget he is even in the film — and as a narrator, he serves no purpose; most of the time, he simply explains the obvious. As a comic-relief, he is simply irritating. Performances are also mixed to say the least — David Bradley is probably the standout, but what he has to work with prevents him from excelling any further; beyond him, I am not remotely impressed. Ewan McGregor, Tilda Swinton, Christoph Waltz and Burn Gorman are all capable of truly exceptional work — but here they are all wasted; and why bother casting someone as skilled as Cate Blanchett in a role that anyone could have played? As for the central child performance, I’m not a fan either — no disrespect to Gregory Mann, who I hope has a long and prosperous career ahead of him, but I find him grating and offputting in the role, with most of his delivery being stilted and inorganic. Overall, an all-star cast squandered. I’m well aware of the unpopularity of this opinion, and it’s not like there’s nothing redemptive here — the animators are obviously master craftsmen who should be commended for their massive efforts, and I appreciate this adaptation taking risks and trying something new with the classic story (though it does amuse me that, even when set in fascist Italy and focussing on the inevitability of mortal expiration, this version is not even remotely close to being as fucked up as the original). I love the concept of Pinocchio having the embodiment of death as a mentor figure, but this — like the other interesting ideas — is never expanded upon in any meaningful way. Plus, the stakes are completely compromised, and goalposts are constantly moved; several frustrating deus-ex-machina moments — like the avatars constantly bending or breaking their own rules and impossible feats being brushed over — prevent me ever taking the characters’ plights seriously. To me, this is an assortment of potentially brilliant individual pieces that can’t form a satisfying whole, with the disparity between the surface-level whimsy and the profoundly unremarkable tedium of the actual content being wider than The Terrible Dogfish’s maw. I totally understand those who extol the former element, but I just don’t meaningfully resonate with anything else.

Guillermo del Toro's Veggie Tales It's interesting to read the synopsis for Collodi's original story in order to see why GDT didn't just render it faithfully. In that version, Geppetto creates Pinnochio in hopes of teaching him to entertain and thus earn a living. Pinnochio rejects his authority first and foremost, and he kills Jimminy Cricket unceremoniously on his way out the door. It's the Disney movie that imparts the story with sentimentality. It's the Disney movie that puts together big musical sequences. Where GDT adheres to Collodi's vision is in making his adaptation instructive. Instead of teaching Pinnochio how to be a proper and productive Italian citizen however, he critiques the forces seeking to exploit him. His take on the picaresque fairy tale is full of obvious biblical allegory critiquing the church, the state, and labor exploitation. These are all things GDT has done before and done better. So what claims to be one man's vision is the work of  Collodi, Walt Disney, and God as well. There's a co-director and a cowriter to consider. This is a lovingly animated hodgepodge, but it's a hodgepodge nonetheless. Too many cooks.

A revisit and reappraisal of this film was not kind to it, for me. I rewatched most of Del Toro’s Pinocchio recently (can’t remember exact date so I’m estimating), mostly out of curiosity over how the film had gotten so much worse in my mind. In talking about it to a friend, I realized I didn’t like it anymore, whereas my initial viewing had left me mostly fond of it though equally baffled by it. Turns out, I don’t really like this movie. It always feels reductive to call a film boring, but I found myself uninterested in large segments of this film’s runtime. The animation is always impressive, in addition to being downright off-putting, and many of the character depictions and designs do a lot to magnify that off-putting sense. The messaging is painfully on-the-nose and heavy handed, even if it’s genuinely interesting here and there because, damn, it isn’t afraid to go to some dark places. And the songs? I hate the songs. I hate them so much. That Mussolini poop song? I’ll say I’m glad it exists, but that’s all, because how funny is it to say to somebody: “Oh, Guillermo Del Toro’s Pinocchio? Mussolini’s in it, and Pinocchio sings a song to him about poop.” There are still some scenes and moments of art design I truly love. And the final few minutes? Poetic perfection.

Acho que das obras do Del Toro (e olha que eu sou completamente apaixonado pela forma que ele vê cinema), Pinocchio, talvez seja a que eu menos gostei, claro, o cineasta tem eu seu currículo obras consagradas como: Pacific Rin, Labirinto do Fauno e a Forma da Água, que são filmes infinitamente melhores que esse aqui. Sinto que ele pode ter sido podado um pouco pela Netflix, por conta de algumas decisões de roteiro que explicarei mais a frente, mesmo assim, ainda é um pouco aquém daquele Guillermo que conhecemos. Eu tentei, tentei demais gostar desse filme, e olha que comecei a vê-lo muito porque eu achava que ele tinha sido um sucesso quando saiu, pode ter sido até, mas infelizmente, não funciona pra mim, e o principal (sem trocadilho) é o principal - Pinocchio, o menino de madeira é chato, tem uma voz extremamente fina que me irrita e, vou pontuar até detalhadamente o último ponto, eu não gosto das desobediências bestas dele, e por mais que eu saiba que ele acabou de "acordar" num mundo onde tudo é novo pra ele, tudo é uma coisa inédita e que ele tem que ver para entender, assim como os sentimentos humanos e até qual é o conceito de morte, eu acho muito subaproveitado aqui, outro ponto que me incomoda durante o longa e o que mais me incomodou na primeira aparição dele, são as músicas, nossa, como são chatas as músicas desse filme, por exemplo, a primeira canção que ele canta, ele perguntando pro Gepeto quais são as coisas e pra que servem, tinha tanto potencial, mas acho ela mal feita, não emociona e não tem nenhum "brio"; e por falar em brio, o único personagem que eu gostei, na verdade, a dupla, foi o Grilo e Gepeto. Eles dois juntos rendem piadas boas, porque é meio que um contra ponto do outro, há momentos muito bons entre os dois, como quando rolam frases como "Ele te ama, seu velho idiota, só que você não vê que ele só quer a sua aprovação, como pai" é simbólico, porque é quando o Gepeto se dá conta que ele não quer o Carlo de volta, ele quer o menino que já nasceu o amando, e são boas as conversas entre "dois velhinhos". Apesar de tudo isso, eu gosto de como o filme nos mostra que o luto nos leva para a decadência, como Gepeto fica após a morte do Carlo, seu primeiro filho, e aliás, já vamos pegar o gancho aqui porque quero colocar o ponto alto do filme e o diretor sabe muito bem fazer filmes assim e me faz chocar com coisas que parecem normais, mas não deveriam ser, esse filme se passa durante o governo de Benito Mussolini, então, você tem um contexto de guerra, em um texto que passa por ele e não é superficial, porque você tem um treinamento, ouça só: de crianças para ir a guerra, crianças emulando um confronto, com um fort, armas e formação. Ponto altíssimo aqui, porque a maioria das crianças nem entendem quando o pai fala "os aviões estão passando" e isso evoca o começo do filme, quando Carlo, filho falecido de Gepeto, vê um avião e fala para o pai romantizando-o "veja pai, é um avião" e seu pai meio que faz pouco caso, porque ele sabe o que significa um avião estar sobrevoando em tempos de guerras: tragédia. Pinocchio é um filme que mistura a fantasia com a descoberta, a morte com a tragédia, o luto com a inocência de uma criança, e que no fim, fica uma lição bonita, abrir mão do que você tem, pode muitas vezes salvar pessoas que você não quer abrir mão.

“Terrible, terrible joy.” Finn Wolfhard trying to be British… Ariana what are you doing here? First off, let me shower the visuals with praise. I adore stop motion and it’s such a good medium with which to tell a puppet’s story. The locations are beautiful and filled with personality, I love the designs of the characters so much. Inside the Whale looks especially impressively gross, but my favourite sequences of the whole movie are the ones in the afterlife with the Blue Fairy, who has a killer design. The hourglasses and the lighting and the hares bantering over cards all feel like they were engineered to appeal to me specifically. So so so cool. Also, using Pinocchio to explore father/son relationships and then how that intersects with the state, especially during Mussolini’s Italy is just such a creative concept and I love it. I do have a few complaints that hold this one back for me. I found it a little irritating until maybe Pinocchio’s first death scene - after that it kicked into gear and I liked it a bit more. It didn’t help that at first Pinocchio was an utter menace, causing more damage than The Cat in the Hat . Like obviously I do not agree with the fascists but they were right Pinocchio needs to lock the fuck in. A lot of the characters kind of grated on me, but they got better after that. The dialogue the whole way through felt a little clunky though. The themes are presented well enough on their own, you don’t need to explain them!!!! As much as I love musicals, I found the songs irritating because the scansion was off and they were all too short to really get a sense of their purpose. Don’t make a musical if you’re not going to fully commit to it!! Criminal that the best song in the movie is saved only for the end credits. Desplat still kills it with the orchestral stuff though, no surprises there. It’s no Pinocchio: A True Story , but it ain’t half bad. Also this would go crazy as a Next to Normal AU.

Front-loaded film that teeters off as it goes on, but I did enjoy it overall. On a technical level, stop-motion animation doesn't get much better than this, but this film's visuals are held back by its art direction. Besides Geppetto, all the human character look lowkey scary, especially Candlewick and Count Volpe (whose design is just repulsive, and not in a good way). Everything else looked great though, including the titular puppet. I'm particularly fond of the "biblically accurate angel"-looking characters (who, much to my amazement, aren't voiced by Cate Blanchett, who instead, voices the fucking monkey). While we're on the topic of voice acting, it was surprisingly not great. No performance stands out as being especially good or especially bad; they're all just kinda okay. Also, the songs really did add NOTHING to this film. I could forgive their lack of relevance if they were actually good songs, but they're not (except for Ciao Papa, which was really sweet, and a major highlight during the latter half of this film). Nothing - I can't believe I'm about to say this - comes close to the quality of the Disney songs. *heaves* *wretches* *gags* Speaking of things that add nothing, I can't understand the Ewan McGregor glazing in these reviews. Bro did assolutamente niente the whole film. To wrap things up, we love ANTIFA Pinocchio, but the story surrounding him is too messy, tangential and episodic-feeling to feel cohesive to me. The emotional moments really didn't hit the way they should've, nor did all the themes this film tries to juggle, even if I could see the vision. I would probably revisit it though, and I'd definitely recommend it for the animation and the novelty of its story and setting.

What Del Toro lacks in subtly, he more than makes up for in heart and beauty. The long-told, well-established story of Pinocchio gets completely flipped around and played with in this 2022 wonder of a watch. I loved how relationship between Gepetto and Pinocchio gets recontextualised with the existence of Carlo (the religious imagery in that one scene being outstanding) & also changing the setting to Fascist Italy?! Sure, that’s kinda fucking rad! If I do have a criticism, it’s that after the first song, the musical numbers just got less and less good (a fact clearly recognised by the filmmakers, as the songs became more and more infrequent to the point of nonexistence). And honestly, that one song did take me out of it a lil bit 😅 BUT, it would be entirely remiss of me not to mention all the things I loved about it too: 1. The stop motion animation art form always boosts the quality of a movie in my mind, they always have a little magic to them and this is no exception. 2. THE CHARACTER DESIGN?! OH MY LORD IT’S JUST FANATASTIC! So many times, I felt my jaw drop to the floor whenever a new character was introduced. 3. STACKED CAST (in a good way). 4. Grief really do hit different. 5. I had a really nice time watching it with Elz. 6. A wonderfully beautiful ending, that can be improved upon in no way, shape, or form. 7. I LOVE YOU EWAN MCGREGOR. And so forth. Fun ol’ watch, and AI could never make something so beautiful and expressive.

Gillermo del Toro has a very nakedly sincere approach to storytelling, its hard not to love him when he expresses this sincerity and passion for life itself in his movies. Pinnochio, both the interpetation of the character and the movie as a whole, is brimming with this infectious love of life, its transparently clear how much talent and effort went into expressing the beauty of fascination with what surrounds us. It was such a lucid decsion to make this with stop motion, to choose an approach that doesnt try to make the author invisible, but the opposite; the whole time you can tell that these are real, delicately crafted objects that somebody took the time to bring life to them, to build them with care and painstakingly animate them, it highlights their efforts without being obtrusive, giving space for the work to breathe. In an age where creativity and imagination are trying to be either buried under the veneer of disinterest or unimportance or commodified for profit, to see something so honest, so loving, so sweet, so kind to the human spirit is to witness a miracle.
