I had an extremely hard time following this movie as so many of the intricacies are so context based and not explained, which I understand is a Japanese cultural difference and it’s sort of my fault for not being able to follow along, but I genuinely think that getting a deeper dive into who the characters were and what the world was at the beginning of the movie and not just throwing you into the story would’ve made the whole thing easier to follow and enjoy without having to change anything else. So that’s really my only complaint, but definitely more of a personal thing. Now that I’ve seen it once and understand, I wouldn’t really want anything changed for a rewatch, and I would totally enjoy watching it again. I think this is one of the most relevant movies I could’ve decided to watch at this time, as I’ve been pondering the exact dilemma in the message. As I’ve been studying international relations and history more deeply, I know that the question of survival between two parties when one side’s existence is dependent on the other not existing is a very prevalent issue throughout history and resurfacing now. And the hatred personified by the demons is the true standout. When humanity is stuck in this dilemma, the most blinding force is a grueling hatred that engrossed people to ignore the obvious environmental clues, like Okkoto blinded to the scouts by the demon, reminding me of the Israel-Palestine conflict. How can both exist, and especially with this hatred? It’s a very relevant message that I think everyone should see. I just wish it were easier to follow so that the message can be driven home more clearly, because I believe that most people (myself included initially) will see this movie and think that it’s just about protecting the environment, and how industrialism etc. and our desire to obtain “everything between heaven and hell” and play god is creating this war between us and nature. Of course that message is true, but it fits into the more encompassing and more important overarching theme I mentioned.

OUR COMPLICATED RELATIONSHIP WITH  NATURE  AND OUR OWN HUMANITY This was my first time watching Princess Mononoke, and I was amazed by how beautifully the film was made and how Hayao Miyazaki brought his imagination to life. It is truly one of Studio Ghibli’s masterpieces, and I would place it as my second favorite Ghibli film, after Spirited Away. The film explores several social issues, but I think its central theme revolves around war, a recurring subject in Hayao’s work. It shows how destructive war can be and how innocent people and other species are dragged into senseless and inhumane conflicts. It also explores how vengeance fuels conflict, suggesting that as long as hatred persists, wars may never truly end. I loved how the film portrayed the destructive effects of human greed and selfishness, not only on nature and other species but also on humanity itself. One of the most interesting aspects was how animals were portrayed as beings capable of hatred and vengeance. They were not simply helpless victims; their desire to defend themselves could eventually evolve into rage, making them capable of hurting humans as well. The animation was exceptional, and the depth and artistic detail of each creature were truly remarkable. The film was also filled with metaphors and symbolism that required close attention. My only criticism was that the ending felt somewhat rushed, leaving me wanting clearer closure. I also feel that I need to rewatch it to fully appreciate the symbolism and details I may have missed. Overall, Princess Mononoke is a visually stunning and thought-provoking masterpiece that explores war, vengeance, greed, and humanity’s complicated relationship with nature.

La princesa Mononoke es una de esas películas que parecen sencillas hasta que uno empieza a mirar debajo de la historia. A primera vista podría parecer un relato sobre la lucha entre los humanos y la naturaleza, pero reducirla a eso sería perder prácticamente todo lo que la hace especial. Miyazaki construye una historia sobre la industrialización, la guerra, el progreso, la marginación, el odio, la espiritualidad y la convivencia, pero sin convertir ninguno de esos temas en una respuesta fácil. Lo más interesante es que no existen buenos y malos absolutos. Los humanos están destruyendo el bosque, sí, pero no porque todos sean crueles o quieran destruir la naturaleza por simple avaricia. Lady Eboshi es el mejor ejemplo. Es quien impulsa la explotación del bosque y quien quiere acabar con los dioses que se interponen en el camino de Iron Town, pero también es una mujer que cree sinceramente que está construyendo un futuro mejor para su gente. Ha creado una comunidad donde personas rechazadas por la sociedad encuentran un lugar. Las mujeres de Iron Town son especialmente importantes. Eboshi las ha sacado de los burdeles y les ha dado trabajo y una cierta independencia, convirtiéndolas en parte esencial de la producción de hierro. También acoge a hombres afectados por la lepra, personas profundamente marginadas en la sociedad de su época, y les permite trabajar y recuperar una dignidad que otros les habían negado. Resulta paradójico que una mujer capaz de ofrecer libertad y protección a personas marginadas sea, al mismo tiempo, responsable de una destrucción enorme del mundo natural. Y precisamente ahí está la grandeza de Eboshi: no es una villana que sabe que está haciendo el mal. Cree que está haciendo lo necesario. Quiere hierro, armas, territorio y seguridad para su ciudad. Quiere que Iron Town prospere. Su problema no es simplemente la maldad, sino la convicción de que el progreso humano justifica conquistar aquello que se interpone en su camino. La película se sitúa, además, en un Japón que está dejando atrás un mundo antiguo. Ashitaka pertenece a los Emishi, un pueblo prácticamente desaparecido ante la expansión del poder imperial. Iron Town representa una nueva época: el hierro, la industria, las armas de fuego y una sociedad que empieza a dominar la naturaleza mediante la tecnología. El bosque, en cambio, pertenece a un mundo anterior, espiritual y ancestral. La película convierte ese cambio histórico en un conflicto entre formas distintas de entender el mundo. Pero Miyazaki tampoco idealiza la naturaleza. Los dioses y animales del bosque son capaces de amar, proteger y sacrificarse, pero también están llenos de rabia. Nago, el dios jabalí, es herido por una bala humana y su dolor se transforma en odio hasta convertirlo en un demonio. Esa misma maldición acaba alcanzando a Ashitaka. Su brazo se vuelve monstruosamente fuerte cuando actúa movido por la ira, pero esa fuerza también lo consume. Es una de las metáforas más bonitas de la película: el odio puede darte fuerza y destruirte al mismo tiempo. Los jabalíes representan precisamente esa tragedia. Quieren recuperar lo que los humanos les han arrebatado, pero su deseo de venganza acaba cegándolos. Okkoto, viejo y orgulloso, termina recorriendo un camino parecido al de Nago. La película deja claro que el sufrimiento de la naturaleza es real, pero también que el odio puede corromper incluso a quienes han sido víctimas. Y ahí aparece Ashitaka. Ashitaka es probablemente el personaje más importante porque no intenta decidir quién merece ganar. Cuando llega al conflicto, intenta comprender a ambos lados. Su filosofía queda resumida en una frase que dice en japonés: 曇りなき眼で見定め、決める。 Kumori naki manako de misadame, kimeru. Algo parecido a: «Ver con ojos despejados, discernir y decidir». La conocida traducción «ver con ojos libres de odio» captura el espíritu de la idea, aunque no sea una traducción literal. Ashitaka intenta mirar sin permitir que el odio, el miedo o los prejuicios decidan por él. Eso es exactamente lo contrario de lo que ocurre con casi todos los demás personajes. San odia a los humanos porque siente que han destruido el mundo al que pertenece. Es humana, pero fue abandonada de niña y criada por Moro, por lo que considera a los lobos su verdadera familia. No quiere volver a la sociedad humana y no necesita hacerlo para que su historia tenga sentido. Ashitaka la ama sin pedirle que abandone aquello que es. Moro, por su parte, sabe que los lobos están perdiendo la batalla y que su propia vida se acerca al final. Sin embargo, continúa luchando por San y por el bosque. Su relación con ella también habla de una idea muy hermosa de la familia: no hace falta compartir sangre para pertenecer unos a otros. Y después está Shishigami. Quizá sea el elemento más difícil de interpretar porque Shishigami no representa simplemente a «la naturaleza». Es algo mucho más profundo. Es la vida y la muerte al mismo tiempo. Da vida, cura y mata. No es bueno ni malo porque la vida misma tampoco funciona bajo esas categorías. Su forma de ciervo durante el día y su gigantesca forma nocturna, el Daidarabotchi, parecen mostrar distintas dimensiones de una misma fuerza. Cuando pierde la cabeza, la vida se convierte en destrucción y todo aquello que toca muere. Cuando finalmente recupera su cabeza, la vida vuelve a brotar. Y aquí llega uno de los momentos que más sentido le da a toda la película. San observa el bosque después de la muerte de Shishigami y dice que ya nunca volverá a ser el mismo. Ashitaka le responde, en esencia, que Shishigami es la vida misma y que, por tanto, la vida continuará. No significa que todo vaya a volver a ser como antes. De hecho, no volverá. El bosque ha sido destruido. Iron Town también ha quedado devastada. Los dioses han sufrido. Personas y animales han muerto. El mundo anterior ha desaparecido. Pero aparecen pequeños brotes. La vida continúa. Y esa es quizá la idea más hermosa de toda la película: la naturaleza no necesita regresar exactamente a lo que era para estar viva otra vez. Por eso el final no es una victoria de la naturaleza sobre los humanos. Tampoco es una victoria humana sobre los dioses. Es una reconstrucción. Ashitaka decide quedarse cerca de Iron Town y ayudar a reconstruirla. San permanece en el bosque. No se «salvan» mutuamente convirtiéndose en personas diferentes. Se quieren, pero respetan que pertenecen a mundos distintos. Es una conclusión sorprendentemente adulta: amar a alguien no significa obligarlo a convertirse en aquello que tú quieres que sea. También por eso Jigo resulta tan interesante. Frente a Eboshi, que realmente cree en su proyecto, Jigo representa el oportunismo. Entiende que el mundo está cambiando y simplemente quiere beneficiarse de ello. Para él, incluso la cabeza de Shishigami puede convertirse en un objeto de poder y riqueza. Es la transformación definitiva de algo sagrado en algo que puede poseerse. Y esa es otra de las grandes tensiones de la película: cuando los humanos dejan de mirar la naturaleza como algo que forma parte de ellos y empiezan a verla exclusivamente como un recurso. El hierro sirve para fabricar herramientas y construir una comunidad, pero también armas capaces de matar a un dios. El progreso puede liberar a unas personas y destruir a otras. La tecnología no es presentada como algo malvado; lo que importa es la relación que establecemos con ella. Por eso La princesa Mononoke no pide que volvamos a vivir sin tecnología ni que abandonemos el progreso. Tampoco dice que los humanos debamos desaparecer para que la naturaleza pueda vivir. Propone algo mucho más difícil: aprender a convivir sin convertir al otro en un enemigo que debe ser eliminado. Al final, Ashitaka no consigue eliminar el conflicto. No consigue que San ame a los humanos, ni que Eboshi deje de construir, ni que el bosque vuelva a ser el que era. Lo único que consigue es impedir que el odio sea la única respuesta posible. Y quizá esa sea la verdadera razón por la que la película sigue siendo tan poderosa. Porque habla de un mundo en el que todos tienen motivos para luchar y, precisamente por eso, todos pueden terminar destruyéndolo todo. Los humanos quieren sobrevivir. El bosque quiere sobrevivir. San quiere proteger a su familia. Eboshi quiere construir un futuro para la suya. Los jabalíes quieren recuperar lo perdido. Los marginados quieren simplemente tener un lugar donde vivir. Nadie está completamente equivocado y nadie está completamente a salvo de equivocarse. Y en medio de todos ellos está Ashitaka, intentando hacer algo aparentemente sencillo pero extraordinariamente difícil: mirar con ojos despejados antes de decidir. Porque La princesa Mononoke no trata realmente de escoger entre humanos y naturaleza. Trata de preguntarnos qué ocurre cuando dejamos que el miedo, el odio y el deseo de poseer algo nos impiden ver que el otro también está intentando sobrevivir. Y, sobre todo, nos recuerda que aunque destruyamos el mundo que conocíamos, mientras exista vida siempre queda la posibilidad de empezar a construir otro. El bosque ya no será el mismo. Pero está vivo.

Não tem muito o que discutir aqui, Hayao Miyazaki simplesmente pegou tudo aquilo que torna o cinema do Studio Ghibli especial e levou para um nível absurdo. É um filme emocionante, inteligente, lindo e narrativamente complexo, capaz de contar uma história de fantasia gigantesca enquanto discute questões muito reais sobre natureza, humanidade, violência e equilíbrio. O mais impressionante é que "Princesa Mononoke" não trata seu conflito central como uma disputa simples entre o bem e o mal. Não existe um lado completamente certo e outro completamente errado. Humanos destroem a natureza, sim, mas também precisam sobreviver. Os espíritos da floresta são fascinantes e poderosos, mas também podem ser perigosos. Cada personagem possui suas próprias razões, e Miyazaki desenvolve seu roteiro afim de compreender essas motivações. O filme consegue falar sobre preservação ambiental sem transformar sua mensagem em um discurso moralista de duas horas. A natureza não é apresentada como algo simplesmente bonitinho que precisa ser protegido porque sim. Ela é poderosa, imprevisível e muitas vezes assustadora. Ao mesmo tempo, os seres humanos não são tratados como uma praga sem salvação. Existe bondade mesmo nas pessoas responsáveis por causar parte daquele conflito. San também é uma personagem maravilhosa justamente porque não pode ser resumida à palavra "princesa". Ela é feroz, determinada e ligada à floresta, mas também é alguém que vive um conflito de identidade e pertencimento. Ashitaka, por outro lado, funciona como uma ponte entre mundos completamente diferentes. Ele não está simplesmente procurando derrotar alguém, está tentando compreender um conflito no qual praticamente ninguém consegue enxergar o outro lado. Miyazaki permite que seus personagens tenham motivos legítimos mesmo quando suas ações são destrutivas. Lady Eboshi, a principal antagonista da história, é o melhor exemplo disso. Ela pode estar contribuindo para a destruição da floresta, mas também oferece um lugar para pessoas marginalizadas e cria uma comunidade onde outras pessoas encontram dignidade. Como você simplesmente olha para uma personagem assim e coloca um adesivo escrito "vilã" na testa? Além disso, "Princesa Mononoke" é lindo em praticamente todos os frames. As florestas, os espíritos, os animais, as cidades, os cenários e até os momentos mais violentos tem uma identidade visual impressionante. Mas a beleza não está ali apenas para impressionar. A floresta é basicamente um personagem (literalmente e metaforicamente), e sua presença muda completamente dependendo do momento da narrativa. Miyazaki consegue fazer você enxergar beleza e ameaça no mesmo espaço, o que combina perfeitamente com a própria mensagem do filme. Não existe uma solução mágica capaz de apagar séculos de conflito para enfim encontrar a coexistência. Não basta destruir o inimigo e seguir em frente. A verdadeira resposta parece estar na tentativa de compreender aquilo que é diferente, mesmo quando essa compreensão não resolve tudo imediatamente. É uma mensagem extremamente humana escondida dentro de uma fantasia sobre deuses, guerreiros e criaturas gigantes. O filme possui momentos de violência e tragédia com muitos detalhes, mas nunca utiliza isso apenas para parecer adulto. As consequências importam. Quando alguém sofre, aquilo tem peso. Quando a natureza é destruída, existe uma sensação de perda real. Quando um personagem toma uma decisão, o filme permite que essa decisão tenha consequências reais. E é justamente por isso que considero esse um dos melhores filmes do Studio Ghibli. Ele possui toda a magia característica do estúdio, mas não depende dela para funcionar. Você pode assistir pela fantasia, pela animação, pelos personagens, pela ação ou pela beleza visual e ainda assim encontrar muito mais coisas escondidas por baixo de tudo isso. É um filme que recompensa tanto a criança fascinada pelo mundo fantástico quanto o adulto interessado nas ideias por trás dele.

I have nothing intelligent to say about this film, not even anything I can disguise as intelligence. All I have is what I thought while watching, which consisted mostly of the thinking equivalent of an eye roll, or a scoff, maybe. When I am watching a film, the defining factor for me—which is a defining factor which builds the basis of “good art,” for me—is whether or not it invokes emotions, & if it does, what kinds of emotions? The amount of symbolism a film saturates itself w/, (this film includes color theory, metaphors, eroticism, babies, & whatnots) does not make it inherently better. Maybe it becomes more interesting in its conversations concerning itself, but it does not, in my opinion, make the film “better.” Rather, I think, a good film is good when it can (a) express emotions about humanity, & (b) do it in an interesting way(do not confuse interesting w/ lots of symbolism). This film does, in my opinion, does not stir emotion, & I didn’t find it particularly interesting in its expressions. For me, if a film has bad dialogue, it really turns me off of it, in terms of my interest in it, which I hope doesn’t make me sound pretentious, but this film didn’t have good dialogue, or rather, it didn’t have dialogue that I enjoyed. Most of the film just felt like one character asking another character a question, & the other says “Oui,” or “No,” & then they make eyes at each other for a solid thirty seconds. Those are the parts that, to me, felt the most hokey. Also, I thought that the characters were very melodramatic, which you could argue is because they’re two gay women experiencing love for the first time, but I feel like that’s just an excuse for bad writing. It’s possible to portray lesbian romances w/o making the characters act totally melodramatic(Desert Hearts & The Handmaiden are two that come to mind w/ my extremely lmtd knowledge). There were some parts I liked. I liked the part where she reads the myth of Orpheus. I thought the abortion scene was very well done(I thought Sophie was a very well done character in general). I like that there were no men in the film, because, like, to put men on the island would totally desacralize it. I like the final scene, with the music performance. &c. Not to mention that—& I know this might be totally solipsistic of me to say—the subjects that the film focus on aren’t exactly in my ball park of experiences, which usually isn’t the case for me. I really enjoyed Paris is Burning, but I’m not a drag queen; I love Allen Ginsberg’s Howl, even though I’m not a gay man in the ‘50s; so why do those pieces of art speak to me even though the experiences are foreign. I think it has something to do w/ those pieces being something more like timeless that this film really isn’t, I guess. If you read this far, I’m sorry.

"Il faut être deux pour être drôle." Un poil trop long. Le scénario est plutôt simpliste mais bien amené, ce qui permet de s'attarder sur les émotions des personnages et de prendre le temps d'explorer les sensations. J'ai bien aimé le fait que les décors soient très épurés, même si, quelquefois, cela donne une impression d'inanimé. Surtout en ce qui concerne la pièce centrale du film : la maison. Les plans de caméra sont simples, souvent rapprochés, ce qui donne une impression de proximité, mais leur répétition amène un sentiment d'ennui. J'ai davantage apprécié les plans en extérieur, plus libres et plus fleuris. Les actrices ont une interprétation des rôles assez captivante, surtout en ce qui concerne Adele Haenel. We did a spin-off, and I ended up with Portrait of a Lady on Fire. I went into this movie completely blind. I didn't know anything about it. The first thing that caught me was how visually appealing it is. Cinematically, I can absolutely see why people praise this movie so much. The cinematography, the framing, the performances, and the overall presentation are beautiful. The story is about two women and the relationship that develops between them. I understood what the movie was trying to say, and I could see the depth of their connection. I've also seen people call this one of the most perfect romances ever made, and some even compared its emotional impact to Titanic. But honestly, it didn't hit me that way. For me, I was watching it as a movie rather than emotionally placing myself inside the relationship. Even during the final moments, when people say the movie becomes extremely emotional, I was honestly just thinking, "How long is this going to take?" That doesn't mean I think the movie is bad. Quite the opposite. I think it's an excellent film from a cinematic perspective, and I'm glad I explored something completely different. I believe this is also my first French movie. But emotionally, it just wasn't for me. Maybe I'm simply not someone who connects strongly with romantic stories, and I've never personally experienced being in love, so perhaps that's one reason I couldn't connect with the relationship on that deeper level. 3.5/5

This movie is an artistic ode to feminism and love • pure and genuine love that has no gender. With a complete absence of men throughout the film other than the last scene, it follows the beautiful story of a painter, a young woman called Hélöise, and her maid, Sofia. With building tension, emotional progression and throughout the most magnificent cinematography it portrays love at its most pure form and teaches us that it takes two to be funny. Hélöise is the lady on fire, Eyridice, and Marianne is Orpheus. It’s quite a foreshadowing, through this Ancient Greek myth, that these two women will eventually have to separate and be left only with the tender memory of each other. They were both the painters and the canvases to each other, slowly developing their emotions and interaction, creating dynamically this portrait together, the ultimate conviction of Hélöise, yet the occasion that prompted this tragic love story. And when I say tragic , I mean that these two were never meant to be together. And when it comes to the question “being free is being alone?” , the answer is no, being free is women helping women and making masterpieces like this.

Portrait de la Jeune Fille en Feu Na solidão, senti a liberdade de que você falou. Mas também senti sua ausência Se o melodrama surge perante o sentimentalismo, sobretudo, a partir do exagero emocional, Celine Sciamma nos entrega o mais puro suco daquilo que o gênero significa. A primeira aparição de Héloïse é completamente carregada pela incógnita perante a quem é esta mulher, encapuzada, apenas abre a porta e se lança ao mundo, poucos passos são necessários para que seu capuz caia e se repouse em suas costas, assim revelando seus cabelos loiros, amarrados em um pequeno e bagunçado coque, todo o ar de imponência que era usado ao se referir a ela cai a partir do momento em que se percebe que ela mesmo que arrumou seu cabelo. Entretanto, a curiosidade por sua aparência não apenas se mantém como intensifica, quem é Héloïse? Poucos segundos se passam até o momento em que finalmente Marianne tem seus olhares voltados aos da jovem, contudo, mesmo após, nenhuma resposta é respondida, os olhos que anteriormente pareciam ser a resposta se mostram ainda mais enigmáticos. Se me for permitido, quero poder adicionar mais uma característica altamente intrínseca ao melodrama: a identificação da finitude do amor, ambas sabiam plenamente que cada traço de tinta que Marianne deixava ao quadro a distanciava mais de Héloïse, que ao pintar o amor de sua vida, estava fadando o fim do mesmo, entretanto, inevitável fim. Portrait de la Jeune Fille en Feu surge como um grande marco não apenas ao gênero, mas a todo o cinema Se Bergman inventou o cinema 2 em Persona, Sciamma aqui inventou o cinema 3

Such an extraordinarily tender film, so slow and gentle, yet without a single second feeling wasted. One particularly striking aspect of this film is the use of silence and ambient sound. Early on this silence feels repressive, almost choking at times. Sound and music is used sparingly, but when it is present it is extremely cathartic. Waves violently breaking on the cliffs allow stolen glances, piano music welcomes brief closeness and intimacy, the thumping of cards brings shared laughter, the drone and sweet hum of the singing crowd a mutual look of tender understanding. Even in their first kiss the silence is too overpowering. However Marianne and Héloïse gradually break down that silence together until it bursts asunder, although not through violent noise, but instead a new silence, not repressive but intimate. Yet still they know that what they have must be fleeting and at times that very silence becomes suppressive, even oppressive, again. Together by the roaring waves they can be real, genuine, together. But not in the quiet false society. In a quiet moment Marianne has her look back, her last shared moment and goodbye. The storm has finally broken. The music at the end allows Héloïse a brief respite from the false life like she was told earlier it would, for her to feel and love and remember, her moments to escape from a society where they cannot be together. I am also a sucker for anything Orpheus and Eurydice related, and I believe this film to be one of the most interesting interpretations of the myth. Beautifully heartbreaking and heartbreakingly beautiful.

Absolute masterpiece. Céline Sciamma!!!

What I love most is how the film tackles patriarchy without ever turning its ideas into speeches. It builds its argument through the way Marianne and Héloïse look at each other, paint each other, and gradually learn to exist as equals. Marianne first observes Héloïse in secret, treating her almost like an object to be studied and reproduced. "If you look at me, who do I look at?" Héloïse reveals that she has been learning Marianne’s gestures just as closely as Marianne has studied hers. The woman being painted has her own gaze, her own interpretation. Being seen becomes mutual, and equality begins when the observer accepts that she, too, is being observed. Consent changes the portrait in the same way. The first painting fails because it is made through secrecy and convention. Once she agrees to pose, the portrait becomes collaborative. Their love may ultimately be constrained by a patriarchal society that has already decided what Héloïse's future should look like, but the relationship itself refuses those same rules. It is built on reciprocity, consent, and recognition rather than possession. And when physical togetherness becomes impossible, art and memory preserve what society could not accommodate, not as a substitute for the life they might have shared, but as proof that it existed and permanently changed them. Patriarchy can dictate the shape of Héloïse's public life, but it cannot completely control how she loved, what she remembers, or the part of herself that survives in Marianne's art.

Portrait of a Lady on Fire (2019) Directed by Céline Sciamma Rating: 10 / 10 | Masterpiece ​Portrait of a Lady on Fire brought me to tears. It is a masterpiece that transcends usual romantic boundaries and clichés, burning down the traditional rules of the genre to create a love story that feels entirely, breathtakingly new. It starts on an isolated island, where a talented artist named Marianne (Noémie Merlant) is commissioned for a nearly impossible task: to paint the wedding portrait of Héloïse (Adèle Haenel), a young woman fiercely resisting her impending arranged marriage. Because Héloïse refuses to pose, Marianne must act as a walking companion by day, clandestinely stealing forbidden glances to memorize her subject's features to paint by night. What begins as a tense game of observation slowly ignites into a smoldering slow-burn of impossible yearning. As their walls crumble, the act of looking transforms into an explosive, deeply reciprocal romance with a devastatingly clear end. Director Céline Sciamma delivers something miraculous by entirely eliminating the male gaze. She actively strips away traditional power dynamics, ensuring the leads are on exact equal footing. The chemistry between Noémie Merlant and Adèle Haenel is electric; their bond, much like the portrait itself, is profoundly collaborative. But Sciamma’s boldest, most brilliant choice is the absence of a manipulative score. She packs every single frame with tangible emotion relying purely on Claire Mathon's luscious, warm cinematography and the visceral, ambient sounds of crashing waves and breathing. It is not just your love story. It explains the crushing tragedy of memory and the inevitability of loss. It brilliantly weaves in the myth of Orpheus and Eurydice, challenging us to understand the difference between making the "lover's choice" and the "poet's choice." Haunted by the ghost of their sizzling final farewell, the film teaches us a brutal truth: the perfect song seldom plays during our most formative moments, and the perfect person seldom enters our lives at the right time. But choosing to remember them keeps the fire blazing long after the romance ends. It is really a gorgeous, devastatingly heartbreaking, and genuinely might be one of the best films I have ever seen. It is a story that is uniquely lesbian at its core, yet its profound meditation on the sting of lost love makes it starkly, beautifully universal. I am surprised to say I am endeared by this animation style— the movie looks quite nice and preserves the signature look of the show while nicely translating its visuals to 3D. Beyond the 2004 original I have not seen any other SpongeBob films, but I have seen that original many times, and clearly so have the filmmakers behind The Search for SquarePants . Many of the visual gags from that film are referenced, remixed, or reinterpreted for this movie, which I don’t have much innate objection to when they’ve been releasing new SpongeBob films at a clip of about one every five years— just long enough of a gap that the children that tuned in for their last effort have very likely outgrown the target demographic by the next. 3–5 years has long been treated as the standard for churn when it comes to IP designed for children, so who am I to judge if a joke that worked for me as a child is reworked for the next generation? What I struggle much more to forgive is the repetition of themes. In this film, the titular ‘Bob strives to be seen as a “big guy”, which is a transparent euphemism for maturity. This echoes the sponge of 24 years prior, who wished to be seen as a man. His journey in both films includes episodes obviously inspired by The Odyssey. He is manipulated into action by a scheming green villain. He briefly travels to the surface world to interact with real-life humans. The story of SpongeBob, forever unfinished, becomes a Sisyphean nightmare about a boy incapable of ever truly growing up— after all, what responsible adult would choose to live in a pineapple?

Ini film SpongeBob bioskop ke-4. Judulnya langsung to the point: SpongeBob mau buktiin dia udah "big guy" dan gak dianggap anak kecil lagi. SpongeBob pengen naik roller coaster "Shipwreck" tapi ketinggian belum cukup. Mr. Krabs cerita dulu dia bajak laut bareng Flying Dutchman. SpongeBob kegeeran, tiup terompet terkutuk, dan ke-summon lah Flying Dutchman versi Mark Hamill. Dutchman bilang: "Mau jadi swashbuckler beneran? Ikut aku ke Underworld, selesaikan tes kedewasaan." SpongeBob + Patrick pun masuk ke dunia monster, siren bergigi tajam, squid raksasa, dan benteng ala video game bernama Challenge Cove. Di sana tujuannya bukan cuma selamat, tapi buktiin kalau dia udah dewasa. Sementara itu Krabs, Squidward, dan Gary nyusul nyelametin dia dari Underworld. 1. Kembali ke silliness klasik Setelah beberapa film spin-off streaming, ini kerasa "SpongeBob banget" lagi. Humor slapstick, pun konyol, dan muka SpongeBob yang dibikin desperation pas kedip doang udah bisa ketawa. Rata-rata 1 joke pantat tiap 5 menit. Dumb, tapi niat. 2. Visual & dunia Underworld Animasi 3D CG nya colorful dan "squishy, gross" kayak series awal. Underworld nya kayak taman hiburan gila: campuran Odyssey, Jurassic Park, dan episode SpongeBob lama. Buat anak kecil ini pesta mata. Buat orang dewasa ini "light dip into an acid trip". 3. Pesan simpel tapi kena Di balik kekacauan, film ini ngomongin nerima diri sendiri: kelemahan kamu bisa jadi kekuatan di situasi yang tepat. Dan "keberanian itu soal hati, bukan tinggi badan". Gak berat, tapi pas buat target anak-anak. 4. Mark Hamill sebagai Flying Dutchman Dia beneran main karakter, bukan cuma cameo "eh liat nih aktor terkenal". Vibes bajak laut hantunya nambah epic ke petualangan ini. Kelemahannya 1. Gak ada yang baru Ini "just a SpongeBob movie". Strukturnya: SpongeBob kena masalah > masuk tempat aneh > belajar pelajaran > pulang. Kalau kamu cari plot twist, gak ada. 2. Terlalu overstimulating buat sebagian orang Enerjinya nonstop. Beberapa kritikus ngerasa lingkungan n worldbuildingnya "sparseness" dibanding film CG lain Thun lalu. Si me preguntan por uno de mis primeros recuerdos en una sala de cine, inevitablemente aparece la primera película de Bob Esponja. La recuerdo con un cariño inmenso, ligada a esos miércoles de cine con mi mamá donde intercambiábamos tapas de gaseosa para conseguir la entrada a mitad de precio. Por eso, mi conexión con esta cinta es, en su gran mayoría, pura y vibrante nostalgia. La película logra rescatar la esencia del humor absurdo de las primeras temporadas de la serie, ese estilo que realmente te atrapa. Bob sigue siendo ese personaje noble, ingenuo y un poco tonto que a menudo es manipulado por los demás, pero que nunca pierde su esencia. Además, el slapstick —el humor de golpes y situaciones físicas extremas— funciona a la perfección; admitámoslo: ver sufrir a Calamardo es algo que, por alguna razón, nunca deja de ser divertido. Es una película redonda para disfrutar en familia. Siempre me ha fascinado cómo integran a actores reales en este mundo submarino; esa estética que parece 'mal hecha' o intencionalmente cutre es, al mismo tiempo, lo que la hace visualmente icónica y brillante. Postdata: Sigo sin entender cómo perdieron la cuenta de cuántas veces mostraron el culo de Patricio en una sola película. xD

Even after giving this another watch, while I do still like it overall, I would still consider this to be my least favorite of the four main SpongeBob movies. And I say that because, as a longtime fan of SpongeBob, it is noticeable that the story does reuse some elements from the previous films (such as SpongeBob wanting to prove that he's not just a kid, which was part of the first film's story, the climax happening on the surface like in the second film, and characters going after SpongeBob to save him, like in the third film). Additionally, the story can be a little predictable at times, since we know that SpongeBob is being tricked by the Flying Dutchman before he reveals it to him. And lastly, like I said in my first first review of this film, the film also repeats the main flaw the first film has, which is sidelining some of the main characters of the show and only focusing on a small number of them. But even with those, there are still things to like about the film. The animation is great, the voice actors give great performances, the fight scenes are good, it has a good amount of funny moments, and it is in general a good movie to watch overall. So even if I'd still say that this is one of the weaker SpongeBob movies, I still like it overall and would say it's worth watching.

If I had a nickel for every time Derek Drymon directed a fourth installment of a movie franchise known for zany and wacky shenanigans of colorful characters that had scripts that took some story elements from the first installments, I would have two nickels! Which isn't a lot, but it's weird that it happened twice, right? I, like a grand majority of people, have had this childlike, whimsical, hilarious, optimistic, loving, and hardworking sponge as a major part of my childhood and have even implemented his way of going about the world into our daily lives. I have watched from the first seasons, all the way up to season 12, and have watched all of his movies up to this point. Sponge on the Run has its genuine moments but is severely lacking in other important areas. Sponge Out of Water was a blast and a half adventure, but the first movie is genuinely one of my favorites, and I don't believe anything could top its humor, animation, story, spectacle, and characterization of these characters we have come to love. I have noticed that every movie was helmed by someone heavily involved throughout the show and its run. The legendary creator, Stephen Hillenburg, for the first movie, the showrunner for the show when Hillenburg left after the first few seasons, Paul Tibbit for SOoW, and the co-developer of the show, Tim Hill, for SOTR. Now we have come to this movie, helmed by Derek Drymon, the creative director for the show in its earlier seasons. I was cautiously optimistic, as I liked Drymon’s direction in the things I've seen, but I was wondering how exactly funny it would be, how exactly the cast would be characterized, and whether the plot could carry a whole movie. They also really wanted to emphasize how this movie would bring back vibes of the first iconic seasons. So they intentionally were trying to raise expectations. How did I like it? I honestly had a blast, just as much as I had with Sponge Out of Water, if I am being totally honest. If I wasn’t laughing at how surprisingly funny and zany it could get with well-timed jokes and slapstick, I was always smiling from ear to ear. I even enjoyed the plot and the story, where the BOB wants to be seen as a BIG GUY and be respected as such by being brave, especially by Mr. Krabs, one of the biggest guys he knows, so he goes along with Patrick to help the Flying Dutchman to the Underworld to prove he is indeed a BIG GUY, who was surprisingly well-acted by Mark Hamill. Not only was the comedy on point for me, but also, I really enjoyed the relationships displayed in this movie, especially the father-son dynamic with Krabs and SpongeBob. Even has a nice enough message, though I do admit it is taking a lot from the first movie and is not as well executed as it was then. The animation, while not as detailed as SOTR, is stylised in a way where it is essentially how the show looks in 3D. While this is not a perfect movie, let alone a perfect SpongeBob movie, I still had a lot of fun and even felt as happy to see SpongeBob on the big screen through this movie as I was when I was a kid rewatching the first filam an the constant reruns of episodes. So in a sense, I do feel it somewhat captured the vibes of the early seasons, just a bit. Well done, Drymon!

Zerre beğenmedim Le Haine 'ı. Hatta film o kadar uykumu getirdi ki, dümdüz duvara bakınca bile uykum açılıyordu. Bana hiç geçmedi ne film, ne de filmin anlatmaya ve vermeye çalıştığı mesaj. Dört saatlik uykuyla tüm gün mesaide olduğumdan mıdır bilmiyorum. Ben mi sığırım diye düşünmeden edemedim. Bu yüzden ileride tekrar şans vereceğim bu filme. Fimi beğenmiyor oluşumun nedenlerini tek tük sayacak olursam: Öncelikle, hikâye inanılmaz minimal. Büyük bir olay örgüsü, merak unsuru veya dramatik herhangi bir gelişmeden çok uzak bir film Le Haine . Bir filmin sizi ekran başında tutması gerekir ya, işte beni ekran başında tutamadı Le Haine . Bana hiçbir şekilde kanca geçiremedi film. Çok bunaldım izlerken. Filmin sinematografisini de beğenmedim. Filmin içerdiği mekanlar düşününce ilgi çekici olsa da, o atmosferin içine giremedim. Hani siyah-beyaz film olmasından dersin ama ondan da değil. Siyah-beyaz çok film de izledim ve beğendiğim de çok o tarz film oldu çünkü. Direkt bu filme özel bir durum bendeki. En kritik noktalardan biri de film boyunca sahip olduğum beklentinin harcanması. Sürekli, " ha olacak, ha bir şey geliyor, hadi olsun artık, " diye diye izledim tüm filmi ve hiçbir şey de olmadı. Filmin finalini de beğenmedim. Tamam vermek istediği mesaj anlamlı ama onu başarılı bir şekilde verememiş bence. Film finale kadar inanılmaz ağır ve hantal, finalde ise apar topar bitirilmiş film. Ben şahsen filmlerde karakter gelişimlerini, güçlü olay örgülerini, içine çeken bir atmosferi, senaryoyla beraber senaryonun ele alış biçimi gibi unsurları arayan bir insanım. Le Haine de beni bu açıdan hiç tatmin edemedi. Saygı duyuyorum filme, sevenleri de anlayabiliyorum; ama bana hitap etmedi.

Je comprends pourquoi ce film du cinéma français a rencontré un tel succès il y a 30 ans et continue de rencontrer ce même succès à l’heure actuelle. Vinz, Hubert et Saïd sont les trois personnages que nous suivons durant les 24 heures qui suivent une nuit d’émeutes provoquée par les violences policières. Le message du film est certainement celui du cercle vicieux de la violence . Face à cette situation, les trois personnalités que nous suivons sont très intéressantes, tant elles sont différentes face à une même situation : • Vinz incarne la vengeance, le désir de contrôle et la haine. C’est d’ailleurs assez symbolique que ce soit lui qui se balade tout le film avec une arme à feu. • Hubert pense, lui, que la violence ne mènera à rien et cherche à quitter cette situation, cette vie qui ne lui correspond pas. • Saïd, lui, observe. Il est un peu situé entre les deux et représente un parfait mélange des deux autres. La scène finale est poignante pour deux raisons à mes yeux : • Vinz se fait tuer au moment où il avait renoncé à cette haine. • Hubert et le policier se pointent mutuellement une arme sur la tête et, à ce moment, l’image se coupe… Le message est : « Peu importe qui tire le premier, le cercle vicieux de la haine a déjà atteint son terme logique. » Personnellement, je ne dirais pas que c’est un film agréable à regarder. Le rythme est redondant, les dialogues parfois dépourvus de sens et le noir et blanc, bien qu’il apporte un aspect hors du temps et une ressemblance avec un documentaire, ne correspond pas spécialement au style que j’attends. En conclusion, je reconnais toutes ses qualités, mais je ne suis pas spécialement touché par le film, ni même par ses techniques de réalisation.

Acting exceptionnel, Vincent Cassel phénoménal. Noir et blanc, une seule journée : 30 ans après, aucune ride sûrement parce que ce qu'il raconte n'a pas changé. Très réaliste : tellement de temps morts comblés par des dialogues et autres que quand la violence arrive, tu la sens vraiment. Le trio est génial, ils s'engueulent mais restent ensemble jusqu'au bout car jusqu’ici tout va bien. Un blanc, un noir, un arabe c'est pensé : la galère n'est pas une question d'origine mais de quartier. « Jusqu'ici tout va bien »… tout le film tient dans cette phrase. Les plans de Cassel face caméra, forts. Les musiques (NTM) qui portent tout. La fin, je m'y attendais mais pas du tout : tu la prends en pleine face. Un des meilleurs films sur les quartiers en France, si ce n'est le meilleur le précurseur de plein d'autres, films comme séries.

Admiro como muitos filmes da época conseguem tratar suas ideias com originalidade e coragem pra seguir seus ideais; La Haine muitas vezes foge da temática central (apesar de se manter sempre com a mesma ideia, mesmo que as vezes sendo secundária) e se propõe, voluntariamente, a desenvolver a relação e personalidade dos protagonistas mesmo que de maneira “avulsa” A atuação e cinematografia é outro fator a se destacar, e ambos andam muito lado a lado em várias cenas do filme, como se um não funcionasse tão bem sem o outro. Apesar de tudo isso, senti que a história quando focava em sua crítica principal batia sempre no mesmo ponto e, principalmente, da mesma forma, como se estivesse em um ciclo; pode ser proposital, mas te traz uma sensação de inércia no decorrer do filme e a mensagem satura um pouco essa mensagem. O final, inclusive, se torna esperado e até “previsivel” de certa forma em decorrência disso.

La Haine ما يحتاج أحداث ضخمة حتى يشدك، لأن كل ثقله موجود بالشخصيات نفسها، بطريقة تفكيرهم، اختلافاتهم، غضبهم، ونظرتهم للحياة والواقع اللي عايشين بيه. كل واحد منهم يمثل جانب مختلف، ولهذا تفاعلهم ويا بعض هو اللي يخلي الفيلم ممتع فعلًا. أكثر شي عجبني إن الفيلم ما يحاول يخليك تشوف شخصية معينة كأنها الصح والباقي غلط، وإنما يخليك تعيش وياهم وتفهم شلون كل واحد وصل لهالمرحلة. الحوار، السكوت، النظرات، وحتى أبسط التصرفات تحس وراها تراكم كامل من الغضب والإحباط والصراع. والتصوير بالأبيض والأسود كان مناسب جدًا لجو الفيلم، وخلى كل مشهد يحسسك بثقل المكان والواقع اللي عايشين بيه. أكو لقطات بسيطة جدًا بس تظل عالقة بالبال، وهذا الشي يثبت شكد الإخراج كان مسيطر على التجربة. الفيلم بالنسبة إلي مو عن شنو راح يصير، وإنما عن شلون الشخصيات راح تتعامل ويا الشي اللي يصير، وهنا كانت المتعة الحقيقية. كل ما تتعمق بالشخصيات أكثر، تحس إن الفيلم يصير أثقل وأقوى

Como descrever esse filme? La Haine é o tipo de filme que você não mudaria nada, absolutamente nada. O filme promete e entrega tudo que poderia ser: uma crítica à segregação, ao racismo institucional, exclusão social de imigrantes e seus descendentes na França e até questões filosóficas, como o existencialismo. O filme acompanha a relação de três jovens, um judeu (Vinz), um árabe (Said) e um negro (Hubert) que vivem numa França pós colonização e dentro de uma periferia, e que nutrem um ódio pelos preconceitos que sofrem na sociedade externa a esse banlieue , principalmente pela repressão policial . O seu estopim, de acordo com o filme, acontece pela morte de Abdel Ichaha, que era um amigo muito próximo do grupo, sendo uma referência direta ao caso de Makomé M'Bowole, um jovem de 17 anos que foi assassinado com um tiro à queima-roupa por um policial. A partir disso, Vinz, um dos membros desse grupo e o mais cabeça quente, num dos protestos que aconteceram após a morte de Abdel, encontra uma arma perdida de um policial. E então a trama gira em torno da sede que Vinz possui de matar um policial para "nivelar o jogo" e o desejo de ser respeitado pela sua periferia. Também somos apresentados com Hubert, a contraparte de Vinz. Se Vinz é o impulsivo, Hubert é o racional; se Vinz é briguento, Hubert, por mais que seja um lutador de boxe, prefere evitar brigas. o papel de Hubert nesse filme é essencial para o desenvolvimento de Vinz, agindo como um irmão mais velho, sempre aconselhando Vinz de que o objetivo de matar um policial nunca será a melhor escolha, porque isso não elimina o ódio, somente nutre. O terceiro membro, Said, age como o mais imaturo/inocente do grupo. Ele é um contraste entre os dois personagens, meio que o meio termo dos dois. Ao mesmo que tempo que Said muitas vezes fica do lado de Hubert nas suas decisões morais, ele também participa dos protestos que ocorrem no começo do filme. A estética muito estilosa do filme, para mim, é o que torna ele um dos filmes mais únicos e bonitos de se ver. Ao decorrer da trama você encontra diversas cenas incríveis, como a cena do Vinz no espelho, a dos três no banheiro com um enquadramento tão foda que fica até confuso, o uso do alto contraste entre preto e branco que aproxima o filme de um documentário real, as atuações, a transição da câmera da periferia para o centro de Paris, entre diversas outras qualidades. O final do filme é o ápice da trama, porque ele reforça a narrativa circular. O filme abre com Said abrindo os olho e termina com ele fechando. Isso acontece porque Vinz acaba entendendo o lado de Hubert e fazendo as pazes, mas na hora de ir embora, Vinz e Said acabam sendo pegos por policiais, e um deles acaba "sem querer" matando Vinz com um tiro na cabeça. Isso reflete na morte de Abdel, por mais que isso contradiga o que eu afirmei no começo, não era o estopim, era só mais um "até aqui, está tudo bem". Com Said fechando os olhos, o ciclo é repetido num loop de uma sociedade decadente. "É a história de uma sociedade que cai, e que repete, durante a queda, como para se reconfortar: Até aqui, está tudo bem, até aqui, está tudo bem, até aqui, está tudo bem. Mas o importante não é a queda, é a aterrissagem." Para mim, a sociedade já aterrissou. Para mim, a sociedade já aterrissou. 10/10

Ce film est une noix de coco, sacrément idéalisé par les "cinéphiles" pour que l'intérieur de ce film à humour noir soit complètement vide. Oui c'est de la satire, oui ceux qui nous commandent sont complètement dépassés et stupide, oui la menace de la guerre froide est remplacée par cette sorte d'humour dérisoire... Mais est-ce que ses arguments en font un bon film ? Absolument pas... Ne me parlez pas de performance d'acteurs, on est bien loin des véritables sensations qu'étaient la paire Kidman /Cruise, du sergent instructeur Hartman et de son homologue psychopathe, sans parler de Nicholson... Pour ma part, Kubrick a raté le coche. Non là, on a affaire à des clowns qui jouent des clowns. Commençons par les points positifs car j'en ai retenu quelques uns... -Primo, les caméras épaules dans les "rares scènes de fusillades" qui sont très violentes et parfaitement réalistes. On est plongé dedans sans trop savoir si on est le tireur ou son homologue voisin, mais on fait partie du groupe. (je ne parle pas du plan contre plongée à l'intérieur du batiment, totalement cataclysmique). -Tout type de plan en dehors de la war room est entièrement crédible. Les scènes d'avions, bien qu'elle soit rare et d'époques, sont plutôt réussi et se regardent sans trop tousser. -Le président américain de moins en moins respecté, c'était plutôt bien joué de la part de Kubrick, l'acteur s'en sort pas trop mal, même si je l'oublierai dans deux jours. Voila c'est à peu près tout en qualité. Que je n'ai pas aimé l'humour noir du film, c'est une chose. Si je passe outre ces 90% du film, bon et bien c'est pas terrible du tout. Les conversations sont pour ma part, de plus en plus redondante et impertinente au fur et à mesure de l'intrigue malgré les enjeux grandissants. Je suis fortement malaisé à chaque prise de paroles de ce général "allemand"... On a compris que tu étais allemand, faire la même blague 2 fois ca va, mais 4-5 fois ca commence à faire... Les appels avec les Russes, enfin... Ce bon vieux Dimitri, pas vraiment grand chose à dire, c'est mou... Une chose qui me désespère vraiment dans ce film, détail certes, mais qui m'agacent au plus haut point, c'est la scène de la fusillade où le colonel américain fait irruption dans le bureau (juste après le suicide). Premièrement, il tient son arme comme un pistolet à eau de 2 kilos... Rend la chose un minimum réaliste stp... On est pas dans les power rangers... La scène qui suit au téléphone, beaucoup trop longue pour peu de rire finalement... Oui j'ai compris les enjeux du film, oui à son humour aussi dans un contexte de tension extrême de guerre froide, mais ce n'est pas un bon film, et c'est complètement oubliable. Je n'en garderai aucun souvenir, et aucune scène... Ah si, je sais maintenant que l'un des antagonistes des indestructibles s'appelle comme ça, en clin d'oeil au film, merci...

C'est probablement l'un des pires Kubrick selon moi. Le film nous propose une sorte de huis clos politique qui ressemble plus à l'ancêtre de BFM TV qu'à un véritable film. Ça parle, ça reparle, ça rediscute encore et encore pour finalement pas grand-chose. Mais surtout, sans que le film ait réellement l'impression d'avancer. J'ai l'impression d'avoir entendu les mêmes discours pendant 1h30, le même message pendant 1h30, les mêmes phrases pendant 1h30 et surtout les mêmes dialogues répétitifs pendant 1h30. C'est clairement l'emploi du temps de BFM TV ! Les acteurs sont très limités, jusqu'à un point où un seul acteur joue trois personnages différents. C'est peut-être la seule véritable prouesse du film, mais malheureusement, même avec le maquillage, les costumes et les changements de personnage, on le reconnaît immédiatement. Ça devient presque ridicule. Le jeu d'acteur est souvent surjoué et mal dosé. Et surtout, l'humour noir et l'absurdité qu'on m'avait vendus sont quasiment absents. On m'avait vendu un film rempli d'humour noir, d'absurdité et de satire. Au final, j'ai trouvé une ou deux scènes réellement amusantes, mais le reste est beaucoup trop sérieux. Ce n'est même pas vraiment une comédie à mes yeux. L'absurdité apparaît peut-être une ou deux fois, puis disparaît complètement. L'humour noir qu'on m'avait promis s'est littéralement fait cracher dessus avant même d'arriver. Et décidément, un huis clos ne pourra jamais faire mieux que 12 Hommes en colère. La tension est artificielle, les rebondissements sont quasiment inexistants et, pendant 1h30, j'ai surtout eu l'impression de regarder un discours politique interminable. Je ne trouve quasiment rien de cinématographique ou de créatif dans ce film. À part une ou deux scènes rigolotes, il n'y a pas grand-chose qui m'a diverti. Et même la musique me paraît, selon moi, plus créative et plus complète que le film en entier. Elle propose davantage d'idées, d'ambiance et de variété que ce que le film arrive à me proposer pendant 1h30. C'est quand même assez ironique de sortir d'un film en ayant l'impression que sa bande-son est plus intéressante que son propre contenu. Mais il y a quand même quelques passages que j'ai trouvés vraiment réussis. Les séquences autour de la guerre, notamment tout ce qui concerne l'avion et son crash, sont particulièrement bien faites pour l'époque, surtout quand on prend en compte le budget du film. Visuellement, ces passages sont beaucoup plus intéressants et montrent enfin quelque chose de réellement cinématographique. Les indications militaires, le contexte de la guerre et tout ce qui touche à la menace communiste sont également plutôt sympathiques. Ces passages sont malheureusement assez rares, mais lorsqu'ils arrivent, ils m'ont presque permis de ne pas décrocher complètement. C'est peut-être même ce qui m'a empêché de passer mon temps à faire défiler une émission politique comme si je pouvais simplement scroller pour passer à la prochaine émission. Bref, un huis clos ultra simple, peu divertissant et, selon moi, particulièrement vide. Une caricature totale. Et surtout une caricature totalement surcotée...

Eu fiz algumas pesquisas e descobri que Kubrick era fascinado pela guerra, não por glorificação militar e sim expor a fragilidade e irracionalidade humana. Em Dr. Strangelove Kubrick usou sua brilhante mente para juntar guerra e sexo em uma comédia. Durante o filme acompanhamos homens incompetentes tentando manejar uma guerra como se estivessem brincando num parquinho. Esse é um ponto que me fez rir, porque a crítica de Kubrick é extremamente real. Nas guerras atuais, ainda notamos os "fetiches" de homens no comando de potências globais se divertindo com o desespero alheio. A masculinidade tóxica pode nos levar (ou já está nos levando) a um futuro ridículo. E de novo, a cinematografia é incrível! O enquadramento dos personagens é crucial para uma interpretação mais perspicaz.

C'est vraiment très intéressant et intelligent, c'est une critique et une satire évidente de ce que les humains font des bombes nucléaires. On y voit le même acteur, Peter Sellers, jouer plusieurs rôles très différents pour montrer que les humains sont, malgré tout, tous assez similaires et bêtes face à un état de paranoïa, de guerre et d'égo. La scène de fin avec la bombe est évidemment excellente également. Mais...ouais, ça n'a pas frappé si fort que ça chez moi. C'est juste triste parce que je ne peux pas vraiment l'expliquer, je me suis juste un peu ennuyée malgré la pertinence du film. Bon, à une prochaine Kubrick, il me reste des films à voir qui me seront, je suis sûre, une immense claque.

“film and american society” watch #3 I cannot tell you how excited I was to finally watch this film, both due to its reputation and the admiration I have for Kubrick as a filmmaker, which is why is saddens me greatly to say I didn’t love Dr. Strangelove: or How I Learned to Stop Worrying and Love the Bomb . On one hand, I think it’s brilliantly written and effectively captures the simultaneously silly, absurd, and terrifying reality of nuclear warfare and the sociopolitical aspects fully in the hands of man. Naturally, it’s stretched to the extreme given its comically outrageous nature, but in many ways, Dr. Strangelove ’s sharp criticisms  remain relevant today: global annihilation, and consequently the fate of the entirety of humanity, is at the mercy of a bunch of horny, overzealous and incompetent men toying around with hydrogen bombs as if they were play things whilst comparing the sizes of their di-I mean missles. And given it’s a satire, I do find much of Dr. Strangelove to be humorous, and I did get a decent chuckle out of me from time to time. But at the end of the day, I really didn’t find this film to be all the funny. I just feel like it’s a tad bit outdated and, at times, too goofy for its own good. I can certainly see the appeal for others and Kubrick’s audience at the time of it’s release, but there were many instances  where I knew I should have been bursting out laughing, but at most was cracking a smirk. And as I’ve said in previous reviews, films focused solely on politics or historical events typically just don’t do it for me, and I think Dr. Strangelove unfortunately falls into that category for me. The acting is great (Peter Sellers in his triple performance and Sterling Hayden in particular are fantastic) and the story is well-written, but it was unsuccessful in fully sucking me into the chaos and panic of this world. I was sadly a bit bored at times (despite a rather short runtime) and was simultaneously hoping it’d keep going so I could get to a part I loved and wanting it to end. This film, in no way, shape, or form, takes away from my feelings towards Kubrick as an artist. As I’ve said before, I do think it’s cleverly written, well-executed, and impeccably shot film (might I add), with cinematography that once again proves he’s second to none when it comes to knowing the camera and where it should go. But the sociopolitical themes and darkly satirical humor of Dr. Strangelove just didn’t resonate or impact me the way I’d hoped they would. It pains me to say it, but this is my least favorite Kubrick as of now.

I finally get why people call Kubrick a genius. I’ve watched plenty of political satires, but seeing Dr. Strangelove makes it obvious how much he paved the way for this genre. The movie isn't just funny; it's terrifying. He forces you to laugh at situations that should genuinely horrify you, laying bare how absurd and dangerous human paranoia gets when it's placed in the hands of powerful people. The most depressing part is how well it holds up. We haven't learned a single thing. Unhinged leaders are still taking the wheel, making you feel like it's a matter of when the bomb drops, not if. Strangely enough, that satire movie is right at my front door. At its core, the movie shows how much of this destruction is driven by fragile male egos and sexual insecurity. General Jack D. Ripper literally starts a nuclear war because he has erectile dysfunction and blames it on a communist plot against his "precious bodily fluids." Weapons become bizarre manhood symbols, and absolute destruction is preferred over looking weak or showing emotion. Even as the world is literally ending, the men immediately pivot to Dr. Strangelove's bunker plan because it guarantees them a harem of ten women each. It’s a brutal reminder that for men in power, war is often just an ego trip, no matter the cost.

An absurdist farce of the highest order. 4.5/5.

2001 : L’Odyssée de l’espace est tout simplement un film de merde. C’est tellement à destination des cinéphiles en recherche de profondeur que ça en deviens absurde . Le réal semble tellement pas savoir ce qu’il qu’on a l’impression que c’est un coup de bluff en mode plus c’est gros plus ça passe. Son film enchaîne les séquences sans réelle unité, avec une cohérence pour le moins douteuse et des ponts entre les événements qui paraissent déplacés. Tout le film je me suis demandé qu’est ce que je regardais, si yavais un message que je comprenais pas donc naturellement je suis aller voir un peu les reviews qui saucaient ce film en faisant “ le meilleur film de tous les temps”” Kubrick prédit l’avenir de l’humanité”. Mais c’est tellement bateau ça me tend y’a aucune vision là dedans juste l’imagination débordante d’un mec random. On a juste l’impression qu’il a écouté sa petite voix tout le long de la réalisation et qu’il a appuyé sur “poster”. Au risque de me répéter ma take c’est que personne aime ce film mais tout le monde veut montrer qu’ils sont meilleur que le reste des gens en prétendant l’aimer Bon après ma phase de hater ya quand même du positif dans ce film : - déjà l’ambiance, c’est réussi on est vrm angoissé à essayer de trouver un sens alors que y’en a pas - ensuite les effets spéciaux qui pour le coup ont vraiment très très bien vieillis je me douterai jamais que ce film a presque 60 ans Fin bref si vous avez du temps à perdre avec un film surintellectualisé ce film fera votre bonheur

I hate that I didn’t like this the first time I saw it. I hate that I disliked it again this time around.  I hated the very ambiguous everything. I hated the 10 minute long takes of a ship in space. And I hated that I hated it because I love Kubrick! This time around I definitely appreciated the cinematography more. But why, why does it have to be so drawn out? I don’t need 2 minutes of black screen for the opening part of the film. Now, to praise some shots: I love the window shots, something is always moving. And how did he film the leopard scene? That was crazy. Other than that though, I thought Kubrick was just flexing what he can do with a camera. The shots are just overdone for my taste. Was the cinematography good? Yes. Was the villain semi decent? Yes! Is this my least favorite Kubrick? YES! Maybe I just don’t get it. But I really just don’t think it’s for me. Still getting the box set though. Edit: I feel like I mostly hated on it in this review so I wanted to come back and say that some of my favorite films as a kid, Star Wars, would not be made along with many others had it not been for this film. And it is a masterfully well-crafted piece of art. Probably some of Kubrick’s best. But it’s not as well-rounded as I find most of his others to be.

As much as I love Kubrick and as much as this is probably the most technically impressive film ever, there’s only so much jerking off to one’s own cinematography that I can take. And I love Barry Lyndon (which I often hear being called boring and style-over-substance by critics), but I think it’s got a super compelling narrative and cast; that film is infinitely more of an ‘odyssey’ than 2001: A Space Odyssey is. What is Kubrick actually trying to say in this? People will say this film explores themes like human evolution and our place in the universe, but it has very little to actually say about it. We watch all these glorious sequences of evolution and vast expanses in space, but what is the point ? I don’t dislike films with unconvential narratives and very little character focus, as long as they are being used to communicate something. But there is very little point to this film other than for Kubrick to revel in his undeniable technical prowess. Boy, I can’t wait to watch Solaris now…

I got in a debate with my mate the other day about the best directors of all time. He made a good point about Stanley Kubrick and the influence he has had on cinema. I have already watched some Stanley Kubrick, notable Full Metal Jacket which I thought was incredible, so I decided to check out more of his work and watch 2001 - A Space Odyssey. What stood out was the visual and practical affects. For a film close to 60 years old, I was definitely surprised by every shot. I liked the use of the rotating cameras while in the spaceships that created a futuristic sense, and can only imagine what that would've felt like to see in cinema when it released. I have to say Kubrick is very creative in this aspect, but the film fell off because of the story and the pacing. It felt like Kubrick was just throwing things into the film because he wanted to, not because they had significant meaning that added to the story. As well as this, I feel like much more emotion could've been portrayed, such as when HAL was being shut down, Dave hardly showed any emotion and was almost as robotic as the computer, which may have been done on purpose, but this choice doesn't have any weight when we don't know his character and personality anyway. Overall this film could have been a lot better, mainly through the story and pacing, which leads me to the conclusion that it is a bit overrated, and seems to be over hyped just because it's a Stanley Kubrick film.

[ my first hot take? ] this film has some amazing visuals, some brilliant and unorthodox shot compositions, and a plot while, not absolutely massively profound, is wonderfully open ended and revolutionary. a film that is absolutely INCREDIBLE for its time, and yet, i found myself listless during this film. i can tell why this film is so important, i can tell it through it's scores and through it's wonderful VFX, i can tell from it's concepts and what it represented, but, at least to me, and maybe to modern standards, this film is brutally slow. i get its showing off, its doing things that have never been done before, but i seriously don't need to see the same sorta sequence of this guy going out to repair something?! it doesn't feel like it's building tension, it doesn't feel as if it means anything more than boasting, and i don't care for that because while it is cool there's a movie i want to watch. don't get me wrong about that last point though, the slow pace was AMAZING sometimes, i loved that wide shot scene of the conference on Clavius and the shots of the news and them having dinner when the main two guys were on the ship. i felt like a true spectator, i love those moments. but when moments are too long it got so boring, like that psychedelic ending sequence, and that main motif that this film's known for is so ANNOYING at times. yes it sounds good, but i don't need to hear it that often. (although that one other sonic motif whenever the monolith's in view is so so wonderful). a lot to like in this film, and though i don't feel it was explored as much as i had wanted it to, i really enjoyed the concept of HAL, i really enjoyed the idea of space travel on demand as if it were regular flight, i liked the videophone and the weird customs identification thing they had, there's a lot of weird ideas and this was probably really exciting to watch with the space race going on and the moon landing happening not too long after this film's release. anyway. definitely not a film i regret watching, but not a film i wanna watch any time soon. it was. so. long.

Yeah yeah, don't worry, I'm putting on the dunce cap as we speak. I was fully anticipating that this movie would be a religious experience, but i was not expecting it to actually reflect my experience with religion. Meaning, I am very glad that there are so many people who find meaning and beauty in it. However, I dont personally see it to that extent, and I feel like the people who do see it that way think that people like me are somehow inferior or blind for not having the same degree of reverence. I tried so hard to see this movie for the masterpiece that I know it is, like purely from an artistic standpoint, and i do have so much respect for it on a technical level. The visuals are insanely good, the horror surrounding the monolith was really effective, and i loved HAL as an antagonist. But I really checked out after the scene with the airlock because I genuinely couldn't reconcile with that level of scientific inaccuracy, even knowing this movie came out before we went to the moon. We knew about the vacuum of space. There's no way they actually thought Dave had any chance of surviving that shit. Not to mention how ATROCIOUS the EVA protocol was. At NO POINT did I see them tether themselves to ANYTHING, they just rawdogged space!!! And I would've forgiven Dave forgetting his helmet if he was in a panicked rush to go save Frank, but these actors are somehow allergic to emoting, so it just came off like he didn't think the helmet was important! What's the point of wearing the rest of the suit, then? Also, and this is where I know people are gonna get out their pitchforks and torches, it was so slow . I know, I know, a gen Z-er with diagnosed ADHD had trouble staying focused, go figure. But I can accept no excuse for how long some of those static shots went on for. Not even for things that were supposed to leave you thinking or moments that let the horror of it all sink in! Just like 45 seconds of a spaceship pulling into a dock! I'm sorry, it took a concerted amount of effort for me to continue to remind myself "this was 60 years ago, cinema was a spectacle back then, the fact that this exists at all is a testament to human innovation". This is my last point and honestly my weakest, but sue me, they could've been a little nicer to HAL. I know this is a huge thematic thing so I'm not actually mad about it, but they spend so much of the movie talking about how HAL is basically just like another human crewmate, but then the first time he makes a mistake they're immediately like "Yeah we gotta kill him". Yes, it was completely unprecedented for him to mess up, but that's how technology and innovation goes. Unprecedented shit happens all the time. Whatever, I guess we just have to immediately assume that he's evil and malicious and not just scared of whatever punishment awaits him for not being perfect. Which is a huge mood btw

My whole review went away twice due to my phone just crashing wtf… trying again now hopefully (on my laptop). Aw man I really don’t know where to begin and usually that isn’t a good sign. I really wanted to love this Kubrick ‘masterpiece’ but it just let me down noo.. I’ll just answer all the questions I got. Is it beautiful? Yes of course, how he went from dr. Strangelove to this within 4 years is beyond me. I can’t deny every scene looks amazing, even if this would come out today it would still be visually stunning. Hell, it even looks better than Star Wars coming out ten years later. I can understand that this was the coolest thing back in the 60's. Are the characters interesting? No, and I don't think they're meant to. The only interesting character is the onboard computer Hal. His whole sequence is the only intriguing part about the whole film, he really carried. How is the story telling? It grabs a very big time period, with big jumps in time for sure, but still pretty interesting. Seeing how an unidentifiable object started our 'smart' human evolution. And is still ruling us millions of years later on. But it is slow and lacks so much explanation. They really tell very little, meant so okay, but the beauty shots in replacement don't do the job enough to keep you engaged. Is it boring? Yes, unfortunately it is. The first act is cool and funny with the monkeys, hiring real people to play in a monkey-costume works really well, but it took a bit too long. The second act about the voyage to the moon is just out and out boring. The third act with Hal, is as said the only really interesting sequence of the whole movie. The end is just confusing and so weird to be fair. Some scenes are very beautiful yes, but taking soo long for fk sake. That really drained me, why do they need to take soo long, pretty boring. Do the themes work? So So. Aliens are fascinating of course, and the idea of another society secretly controlling ours is intriguing. I really liked that realisation came on very late, that was smart and adds to the story for sure, but there was very little explanation, missed chance in my opinion. Is there a final plus? Yes for crying out loud, the score in this film is impeccable! It is the only thing keeping the space shots bearable, but still they take so long even the music can't carry to keep you invested anymore. I think I’m just a bit frustrated. I believe anyone hyping up this movie has to be watching this through their 60's glasses. For then this would be incredible, but now this is just a snoozefest for too much of the film. I'm mostly just dissapointed it didn't live up to the high everyone was talking about. I waited until I would have time to watch this and be invested for it, but it still took me two days/sessions to finish this, because the 20-60 minute timeframe is soo long and boring. All with all, yes I would be open to watch this in a theatre, I think the visuals would definitely win me over more, together with the loud music it could for sure change my opinion in a good way. But for now on a TV it was just not interesting enough. Thanks Hal for carrying somewhat, for god's sake. 3*

The desire to show the genius-innovations of shots makes it feel less like a film, and more like a cinematographer's demo reel. I think in this age of AI, this plot is very much relevant; so I would argue the film still is important today. It definitely deserves respect for the impact it had on filmmaking as a whole. But as much as it's uncomfortable to go against the grain on a Kubrick film review, I believe there is a difference between an "impressive" film and an "enjoyable" one. And without the latter half, it falls short from being a "great" one.

Há uma poderosa força em sua contemplação, onde a imagem fala mais do que qualquer palavra seria capaz de expressar. Gosto de como essa palavra se encaixa na visão de ambas as mídias artísticas que compunham a história de 2001. Em especial, diria que se tornou um dos filmes mais lindos que eu já vi, e justo por assim dizer, conseguindo demonstrar atenciosidade num espaço dedicado a dialoga suas ideias de forma escrita e, principalmente visual. Faz-se pertinente as configurações meticulosas em som, ambiente, e filmagem para elevar a magnitude de seu tema. Envoltos por características exteriores que compõe os sentimentos que nos fazem ser quem somos; ao mesmo tempo, servidos para serem alvos da racionalização maquinal diante a esses sentimentos. A conectividade e solidão, a fraqueza e fortitude, a perplexidade e o assombro, mesmo dicotômicos trabalham enraizados para essa formação humana. Com a evolução, mais acaba se perdendo a rotação dessas características em prol da busca pela perfeita maneira de pensar, agir, ser. HAL, por mais que uma máquina, adquire suas próprias perspectivas como a de uma criatura sem erros; ou melhor, que quando erra, realoca o equívoco para a humanidade imperfeita. Suas pautas existenciais são regidas nesse olhar contemplativo, nos encarregando de descobrir sobre esse entorno denominado vida. E nisso Kubrick se distancia das produções convencionais ao colocar o espaço como seu ponto reflexivo. O desconhecido como uma lembrança vívida no rompimento do lugar-comum. Ainda que compreende o valor de sua imagem, o contentamento ambiente pode trazer menos atenção a detalhes que a própria história carrega em seu texto para salientar, de fato, sua odisseia com glamour. Como alguém que veio do livro antes de ver o filme - ainda assim sendo uma excelente perspectiva sobre a história como um todo - percebo que algumas pontualidades quando trazidas a tela iriam transmitir certas ideias que iconograficamente reduziram a sua significância. littéralement la définition d’une prouesse technique. la mise en scène est absolument dingue, les effets spéciaux sont à l’image de cette prouesse, notamment la représentation de l’espace qui est juste folle, tout le long du film on se retrouve emportés dans une expérience visuelle hallucinante avec des images magnifiques. L’odyssée De L’espace reste malgré tout lent dans sa construction et son rythme ce qui dérange logiquement une grande partie du public mais lorsque qu’on s’immerge vraiment dans le film, cette lenteur ne semble pas du tout pesante et devient même agréable puisqu’elle permet de réellement entrer dans cette expérience en profitant des images splendides . pour revenir sur la mise en scène, les plans sont d’une beauté folle et il ne faut évidemment pas oublier les mouvements de caméra hypnotisants qui nous font réellement ressentir la pesanteur de la station, j’ai aussi beaucoup apprécié la très bonne gestion du silence accentuant la tension omniprésente, on peut évidemment aborder le sujet des musiques qui sont aujourd’hui iconiques et qui nous marquent lors du premier visionnage par leur sensation de donner aux images cet aspect toujours plus grandiose. durant tout le film Stanley Kubrick prend le temps de nous montrer les choses sans pour autant nous les expliquer nous laissant dans le flou et dans le trouble, notamment avec sa fin marquante, je suis amoureux de ce que produit cet homme. en bref, pour un film de 1968 il n’a absolument pas mal vieilli, au contraire vu le contexte actuel avec l’IA etc qui peut remettre en question cette légitimité dans son utilisation, c’est sans aucun doute l’un des plus grands films de tous les temps, ma review est même pas à la hauteur de ce chef d’œuvre.

2001 é a melhor leitura sobre a humanidade na evolução; a forma como é impressa as diversas questões humanas é única eu me questiono o pq dos atos humanos serem considerados extranaturais: os primatas carregam a busca por consciência - sentido - recursos, travam guerras, formam oposições intraespecíficas, competem por seu lugar ; o ser humano se empodera da consciência para procurar mais informações sobre a vida, sobre o universo - a saída do homem da Terra - forma relações, busca poder, domina conceitos através da inteligência - artes marciais, manipulação de alimentos, saúde e bem-estar físico; a preocupação ainda é defender os seus vínculos sociais, ainda há oposições, em nenhum momento perdemos os princípios que os primatas carregam… monólito existe uma falha na maior das criações humanas - a humanização da inteligência artificial - HAL 9000 é um infalível, perfeito e representa o suprassumo da tecnologia com um adicional que são os sentimentos humanos - falhos e imperfeitos evidente no momento em que a inteligência artificial apresenta o mesmo comportamento egoísta, injusto e em que seus interesses sobrepõem a vontade geral - assim como fazem os humanos, assim como fazem os primatas, assim como é a natureza; monólito o homem continua envelhecendo apesar de tudo, continua acumulando riquezas, continuar errando; não existe um fim, buscar por sentido é tão eficiente quanto quebrar ossos com ossos; monólito assim como falou zaratustra, o ser humano é superado, o cognoscível é atravessado, a evolução não é interrompida; uma nova forma é estabelecida, mas, apesar da “superioridade”, não há ruptura com a Terra. pra mim isso é muito natural; a arte é interpretativa e, além da performance, a fotografia de Kubrick é de cair o queixo, sem dúvida um dos melhores filmes já criados;;;;
